...and sing it as a song. That which was spoken as **"Mala-aje"** and so forth is just that. **"Kollairi"** is the head. **"Bolla"** is the syllable **HAM** that abides there. **"Mummu"** is the vision. **"Kakkola"** is the syllable **AM**. The yoga of those two is **"Ghana,"** which is uninterrupted. **"Kripida"** is the indestructible sound. **"Vajja"** is the arising of all that. **"Karuni"** is the practitioner <term>Yogi</term>. **"Kaiaai"** means not doing. **"Narola"** means not performing external union. **"Tahivila"** is one's own entity. **"Khajjaai"** means "one should make oneself unobservable." **"Maanabijaaai"** means "one should drink the drink of great bliss born from yoga." **"Kalinja"** is the wind <term>prana</term>. **"Pani-aai"** means by entering inside. **"Dudhura"** refers to the afflictions such as attachment. **"Causama"** is the aggregate of form. **"Kacchuri"** is feeling. **"Sihla"** is perception. **"Kapura"** is consciousness. **"Laiaai"** means "causing to join." **"Mala-indhana"** is the aggregate of mental formations. **"Salija"** is the nature of the pride of "I" in all things. **"Taham"** means there the practitioner should eat, meaning they should be made to have no self-nature.

**"Premkhana-kheta"**: the descent of the Bodhicitta fluid from great bliss is called **"Premkhana,"** and its re-entry is called **"Kheta."** **"Shuddha-Ashuddha"** means the point of not knowing existence and non-existence. For that very reason, **"Ramsu"** is a drop of fluid, due to having a similar nature. By that, **"Ambha"** means it should be placed in the channel-limbs of the body. **"Tahim"** means by such a union. **"Sarava"** is Nairatmya, the selflessness of all phenomena. **"Paniaai"** means "should be followed." **"Malayaja"** is the assembly of the channels.

B.text:
The song should be sung. This is expressed in the phrase <term>malaya-ja</term> <gloss>born of the Malaya mountain/sandalwood</gloss> and so forth. <term>Kolla-iri</term> refers to the head. <term>Bolla</term> refers to the syllable <term>ham</term> which resides there. <term>Mumuni</term> refers to the gaze. <term>Kakkola</term> refers to the syllable <term>am</term>. The union of these two is <term>ghana</term>, meaning uninterrupted flow. <term>Kripita</term> is the indestructible sound. <term>Vajja</term> refers to the arising of all these. <term>Karuni</term> refers to the practitioner <note>yogin</note>. <term>Ka-a-i</term> refers to non-action. <term>Narola</term> refers to not engaging in external meditative absorption. <term>Tahin-bila</term> refers to the nature of selfhood. <term>Khajja-i</term> means that the self should not be observed <note>the realization of selflessness</note>. <term>Ma-ana-vija-a-i</term> means one should drink the drink of great bliss born from yoga. <term>Kalinja</term> refers to the vital wind <note>prana</note>. <term>Pani-a-i</term> refers to the wind entering inside. <term>Dudhura</term> refers to the afflictions such as attachment. <term>Causa-ma</term> refers to the aggregate of form. <term>Kacchuri</term> refers to the aggregate of feeling. <term>Sihla</term> refers to the aggregate of perception. <term>Kapura</term> refers to the aggregate of consciousness. <term>La-i-a-i</term> means to bring into union. <term>Mala-indhana</term> refers to the aggregate of formations. <term>Salija</term> refers to the nature of the pride of the self in all things. <term>Taham</term> means the practitioner should eat there, which means to make things natureless <note>void of inherent existence</note>. <term>Prenkhana-kheta</term>: <term>prenkhana</term> refers to the flow of the liquid bodhichitta from the state of great bliss, and <term>kheta</term> refers to its re-entry. <term>Shuddha-ashuddha</term> means not perceiving things as existing or non-existing. Therefore, <term>ramsu</term> is used because of its correspondence to that; <term>ramsu</term> refers to the drops of fluid. By that, <term>ambha</term>, which refers to the channels of the limbs of the body, should be arranged. <term>Tahin</term> means by such a union. The selflessness of all phenomena is <term>sarava</term>. <term>Pani-a-i</term> means that one should follow accordingly. <term>Malaya-ja</term> refers to the gathering of the channels <note>nadis</note>.

<summary>This page provides a coded commentary on Vajrayana terminology, decoding "twilight language" (sandhyabhasha) terms into their yogic and philosophical meanings. It maps various syllables and symbolic words to anatomy, the five aggregates, and internal energy practices.</summary>
<keywords>twilight language, sandhyabhasha, yogic anatomy, five aggregates, bodhichitta, channels, great bliss, selflessness</keywords>

Vairochana. Slander is Ratnasambhava. Passion is Amitabha. Envy is Amoghasiddhi. Regarding **"Pukkasi"** and so forth: Pukkasi, Shavari, Chandali, and Dombini correspond to anger, ignorance, slander, and passion. Furthermore, **"Gauri"** is the Protectress. Gauri, Chauri, Vetali, and Ghasmari correspond respectively to anger, slander, ignorance, and passion. Through ignorance, she is the Earth-Farer. Through passion, she is the Sky-Farer. The word **"by desire"** means after knowing devotion.

To show the answer to the third question, **"Ali"** and so forth was spoken. The first **"Ali"** is the letter **A**. **"Nairatmya"** is the seed syllable of Nairatmya. To show the answer to the fourth question, the phrase **"From the chapter on lineages"** and so forth was spoken. **"Spoken"** means demonstrated. **"Two sixteens"** means thirty-two; for each pair of the thirty-two channels <term>nadi</term>, there is one yogini. **"In successive order"** means exactly according to the sequence. The three channels starting with **Lalana** and **Rasana** are called the "Nairatmya Yoginis." Thus, fifteen yoginis are shown by implication. **Geha**, **Chandika**, and **Maradarika** are the Sky-Farer yoginis. If half of thirty-two is sixteen, one might ask how there come to be fifteen yoginis. For that reason, it was said:

**With effort, abandon the remainder of all.**

This means the final portion of all should be abandoned; the meaning is that this is not the essence of the yogini. If one asks how that is: **"Because the sixteenth has no part,"** and so forth was spoken. **"Doing no purpose"** means not performing the function of the purpose. For example, while the fifteen days of the waxing moon perform the function of illustrating the increase of the moon's light, the sixteenth does not, as it becomes the cause of waning. Therefore, it should be abandoned with effort. If one asks what happens by that:

...is Vairochana <note>The Enlightened One, the central Buddha of the five families</note>. Slander is Ratnasambhava <note>The Jewel-Born Buddha</note>. Attachment is Amitabha <note>The Buddha of Boundless Light</note>. Jealousy is Amoghasiddhi <note>The Buddha of Unfailing Success</note>. Regarding the phrase "the <term>Pukkasi</term> <gloss>a low-caste female deity</gloss> and so forth": the <term>Pukkasi</term>, <term>Shavari</term>, <term>Chandali</term>, and <term>Dombini</term> <note>These four represent classes of yoginis or female spirits often associated with the outskirts of society</note> correspond to hatred, delusion, slander, and desire respectively.

Furthermore, <term>Gauri</term> <gloss>The White One</gloss> is the protectress. For <term>Gauri</term>, <term>Chauri</term>, <term>Vetali</term>, and <term>Ghasmari</term>, they correspond respectively to hatred, slander, delusion, and desire. Through delusion, one becomes a "Stalker of the Earth" <note>A class of female spirit or yogini active on the terrestrial plane</note>. Through desire, one becomes a "Stalker of the Heavens" <note>A celestial yogini or <term>Dakini</term></note>. The phrase "through desire" means having understood devotion.

To provide the answer to the third question, the text says "the <term>Ali</term> <gloss>the series of vowels in the Sanskrit alphabet</gloss> and so forth." The first <term>Ali</term> is the letter A. "Nairatmya" <gloss>The Lady of Selflessness</gloss> refers to the seed-syllable of the deity Nairatmya. To provide the answer to the fourth question, the text says "from the chapter on the families and so forth." The word "spoken" means it was taught.

"Two times sixteen" refers to the thirty-two <note>Thirty-two subtle channels or energy centers in the body</note>. For every two of these, there is one <term>Yogini</term> <gloss>female tantric practitioner or deity</gloss>. The phrase "in successive order" means following the proper sequence. The three channels starting with <term>Lalana</term> <gloss>the left subtle channel</gloss>, <term>Rasana</term> <gloss>the right subtle channel</gloss>, <note>The third is Avadhuti, the central channel</note> are described as the <term>Yogini</term> Nairatmya. This effectively demonstrates the fifteen <term>Yoginis</term>. The channels <term>Geha</term>, <term>Chandika</term>, and <term>Maradarika</term> are the celestial <term>Yoginis</term>.

If half of thirty-two is sixteen, one might ask: how do they become fifteen <term>Yoginis</term>? For this reason, the text says "strive to abandon the remainder of all and so forth." One should abandon the final part of all. This means that the last part is not of the same essence as the <term>Yoginis</term>. If one asks why, the text says "because the sixteenth has no part and so forth." By "not performing a function," it means it does not perform a meaningful action. For example, the fifteen days of the waxing moon perform the function of illustrating the increase of the moon's light. The sixteenth day does not, for it becomes the cause of the moon's waning. Therefore, one should strive to abandon it. If one asks what results from this: the Bodhichitta...

A.text:
she is none other than Nairatmya. That itself is the "mandala wheel." Regarding **"That itself is selfless,"** if one asks what its reality is, it is said: **"having the nature of the sphere of phenomena <term>dharmadhatu</term>."** This is the answer to the five questions. When it says **"Vajragarbha petitioned,"** what did he petition? It is the meaning of the summary <term>samvara</term>. **"Remaining in the center of the yogini's body,"** and so forth was spoken. The "center of the body" is the navel. **"The form of the letter E"** is the first vowel. **"Abiding"** means always residing there.

To show the meaning of the summary, **"Just as externally"** and so forth was spoken. The meaning is: just as the external Nairatmya is meditated upon, so it is here. The meaning is that it is not inferior to that. The intent is that because it is gathered into the body, it is a "summary." Furthermore, here, just like the mandala of Nairatmya, so too is the letter **A** residing in the navel. Just as the letter **A** residing in the navel is the summary of Nairatmya, so too is the letter **HUM** in the "Vajra Sense-Base." The intent is that by the method itself, it is the summary residing in the heart of the Method, Hevajra.

If one asks what happens by that, **"Vajra bliss"** and so forth was spoken. The intent is that the bliss of those two letters reaching the "Vajra Tip" is the cause of accomplishing the body of Mahamudra; therefore it is called **"Mahamudra."** Regarding **"By this"** and so forth, the **"secret union"** is the meditative union of the inner self. If one asks if there is an example for this, **"The two of the two external ones"** was spoken, which refers to the union of Nairatmya and Heruka. Regarding **"The three bodies"** and so forth, the "three bodies of the Buddhas" are the three kayas. It should be said that they reside within the body of the yogini. The full knowledge of the three is the "Essence Body" <term>Svabhavikakaya</term>, which is the nature of the knowledge of equality. It is the "Wheel of Great Bliss." This means the form of the summary of the three bodies is shown in the form of the Wheel of Great Bliss.

B.text:
She herself is <term>Nairatmya</term> <gloss>She Who Has No Self</gloss>. That very essence is the meaning of the phrase "mandala circle." If one asks what the reality of this "Selfless One" is, it is said that she possesses the nature of the <term>dharmadhatu</term> <gloss>sphere of ultimate reality</gloss>. This is the answer to the five questions.

When it is said, "Vajragarbha requested," what did he request? He requested the meaning of the <term>samvara</term> <gloss>union or binding vow</gloss>. Regarding the statement "situated in the center of the body of all yoginis," the center of the body refers to the navel. The phrase "in the form of the letter E" refers to the first vowel. "Abiding" means to dwell there eternally.

To demonstrate the meaning of the union, the text says, "Just as it is externally," and so forth. This means that just as one meditates on the external Nairatmya, the internal is no different. The intention is that because it is condensed within the body, it is called a "union." Furthermore, just as the mandala of Nairatmya is here, so too is the letter A situated at the navel.

Just as the letter A at the navel is the union of Nairatmya, the "Vajra Sense-base" refers to the letter <term>Hum</term>. The intention is that "by means of the method itself," the method is the union abiding in the heart of <term>Hevajra</term> <gloss>Joyful Vajra</gloss>.

If one asks what results from this, the text mentions "Vajra bliss" and so forth. The intention is that the bliss of those two letters reaching the tip of the vajra becomes the cause for accomplishing the body of <term>Mahamudra</term> <gloss>the Great Seal</gloss>; therefore, it is called Mahamudra.

Regarding the phrase "by this," the "secret absorption" refers to the absorption characterized by the internal self. If one asks for an example of this, the text says "the two of the external two," which refers to the union of Nairatmya and Heruka.

Regarding the "three bodies" and so forth, the three bodies of the Buddhas are the three <term>kayas</term> <gloss>dimensions of awakening</gloss>. These should be described as abiding within the body of the yogini. Complete knowledge of these three is the <term>svabhavikakaya</term> <gloss>essential nature body</gloss>, which is the essence of knowing things in their state of equality. This is the meaning of the "wheel of great bliss." The form of the union of the three bodies exists as the wheel of great bliss.

<summary>This page explains the internal tantric anatomy where the deity Nairatmya and the letter A reside at the navel, while Hevajra and the letter Hum reside at the heart. It describes the union of these energies as the cause for achieving Mahamudra and the manifestation of the three Buddha bodies within the practitioner's own body.</summary>
<keywords>Nairatmya, Hevajra, Mahamudra, three bodies, dharmadhatu, navel chakra, secret absorption, yoga tantra</keywords>

A.text:
**"Mountaineer woman, grant the accomplishment of the fruit!"** means "Accomplish the intention of me, Shavarī." Then Chaṇḍālī says, **"Inviter of the world's guests..."** **"Chief of Joy"** means "O chief of intense passion!" **"Emptiness"** refers to the state of having melted. **"Residing"** means staying; it asks "Why?" **"I, Chaṇḍālī, make this request"** means "I, Chaṇḍālī, am praying to you." **"The direction without you is not desired"** means "If you do not remain, the direction in which sentient beings are to be liberated from suffering is not known/desired."

Then Dombī says, **"O You who possess the magical illusion, arise!"** If he were to say, "I am not like a magician," she says: **"I know your mind,"** meaning "I know your own mind." **"I, Dombī, know the clever woman"** means "I, called Dombī, am clever; I know the city-woman" <note>likely an idiomatic expression for being worldly-wise</note>. **"Do not cut the flow of compassion"** means cutting the flow of compassion; it means "Do not remain in the essence of the fluid."

Now, having arisen from the <term>samādhi</term> of the fluid, in order to describe the hand symbols of the Blessed One in his sixteen-armed form, the text says: **"Elephant, horse, donkey..."** and so forth. **"Sharaba"** is a lion. **"Cat"** is a cat. **"Two-drinker"** refers to the elephant and so forth. **"Fire"** is the majestic one. **"End-maker"** is Yama. **"Wealth-giver"** is the son of Vaishravana <note>Kubera</note>. The passage beginning with **"Flirtatious and..."** describes the dancing gait endowed with the nine dramatic sentiments <term>rasa</term>. Now, to show the arising from the <term>samādhi</term> of melting after the exhortation, the text says: **"By AM and HUM..."** and so forth. On top of the moon and sun disks produced from the transformation of the <term>samādhi</term> of melting, the transformation of AM and HUM...

B.text:
<meta>This page continues the commentary on the esoteric union and the transformation of the deity within the tantric practice, specifically focusing on the interactions between the yogini and the central figure.</meta>

Must be practiced! The phrase **"May the Mountain Hermitess <note>Sanskrit: Śabarī</note> accomplish the fruit"** means that I, Śabarī, should accomplish the intended purpose. Then, the **"Fierce Untouchable Woman"** <term>Caṇḍālī</term> <gloss>the inner heat or a specific yogini type</gloss> speaks of hosting the worldly guests. The phrase **"Chief of Joy"** means: "O, the primary leader of intense passion!"

**"Emptiness"** <note>Sanskrit: śūnyatā</note> refers to the state of having become melted <note>the dissolution of the essence in the central channel</note>. **"To reside"** means to remain. For what reason? The phrase **"I, Caṇḍālī, offer a prayer"** means: "I, Caṇḍālī, make a formal request." **"If you are absent, I do not seek that direction"** means: "If you do not remain, I do not seek the direction of acting to liberate sentient beings from suffering." Then, the **"Low-caste Woman"** <term>Ḍombī</term> says: **"O you who possess the power of illusion, please arise!"** This means: "O one possessing the optical illusion <note>Sanskrit: māyā</note>, stand up!"

If one asks, "What if I am not like an illusionist?" then the text says: **"I shall know your mind,"** which means: "I myself shall know your very mind." The phrase **"I, the Ḍombī woman, seek the skillful one"** means: "I, the one called Ḍombī, am the skillful woman; know that I do not belong to the ordinary city." **"Do not let the stream of compassion be cut off"** means: "Interrupting the stream of compassion; do not let it remain only in the nature of the vital fluid <term>śukra</term>."

Now, having arisen from the meditative absorption of the vital fluid, the Blessed One <term>Bhagavān</term> appears in a sixteen-armed form. To describe the hand-implements, the text mentions **"Elephant, horse, donkey,"** and so on. **"Śarabha"** <note>a mythical eight-legged creature</note> means a lion. **"Cat"** means a cat. **"Twice-drinker"** means an elephant and similar animals. **"Fire"** refers to the radiant one. **"The Ender"** refers to Yama <note>the Lord of Death</note>. **"Wealth-Giver"** refers to Vaiśravaṇa <note>the God of Wealth</note>. By the phrase **"Acting with charm,"** and so forth, the text describes the dance movements possessing the nine dramatic sentiments <term>navarasa</term> <gloss>the nine moods of classical Indian aesthetics</gloss>.

Now, following the exhortation, to show the arising from the meditative absorption of melting, the text says: **"By Oṃ and Hūṃ,"** and so on. Upon the disks of the Moon and Sun, which have arisen from the complete transformation of the meditative absorption of melting, the syllables **Oṃ** and **Hūṃ** completely...

<summary>This page provides a commentary on tantric verses involving figures like Caṇḍālī and Ḍombī, interpreting their dialogue as metaphors for the movement of inner energy and the transformation of the deity from a state of dissolution into a manifest sixteen-armed form.</summary>
<keywords>Caṇḍālī, Ḍombī, śūnyatā, compassion, śukra, sixteen-armed deity, navarasa, meditative absorption</keywords>

A.text: Regarding **"Then..."** and so forth: **"How it will be"** means "of what kind." **"Smoke-ink made from great honey"** is the ink of great honey. **"Unfortunate"** means one who has become hateful. **"No accomplishment"** refers to the practitioner. **"The other world"** is another birth. **"Endowed with perfect giving"** means having great devotion to Hevajra. **"Only occasionally"** means shown at certain times. **"Domain of the path"** means the time of walking on the path. **"Shown"** means having been revealed. By the word **"eating,"** the rituals of conduct with elaboration and the Feast Circle and so forth are also shown. **"Where it is eaten"** means during the Feast Circle and the performance of conduct. **"All desired goals"** is the accomplishment of the Great Seal <term>mahāmudrā</term>. To show the distinctions of the places of practice: **"Cemetery..."** and so forth is spoken. **"Mountain over-hang"** is a mountain cave. **"And nine"** is the examination of nine. **"Commitment"** refers to <term>GO KU DA HA NA</term> <note>code for the five meats</note> and so forth. **"After eating, again..."** and so forth. **"Mothers"** refers to the parts of the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; they are to be definitely worshipped with dance, song, and appropriate things. To show that very point: **"Even if it is a mother or sister..."** and so forth is spoken. By the words **"mother"** and so forth, the five sense faculties are spoken; they are to be satisfied by the five sensory qualities of form, sound, smell, and so forth. For the goddesses residing in those places, this is a supreme worship. If you ask how it would be if they were not the eyes and so forth: so it is said in the *Buddha-Skull* <term>Buddhakapāla</term> Yogini Tantra: "Then, explaining correctly: the impure mind must be purified. The eye is the sister; the sister's daughter is the ear; the nose is the progenitor mother; likewise, the tongue is the daughter; the mind is the wife. By these five supreme divine substances, the Great Seal is perfectly bestowed." Thus it is spoken. **"From well-worshipping..."**

B.text:
Concerning the phrase, "then," and so forth: the phrase, "how it will be," means "what it is like." "Ink made from great honey smoke" refers to the ink of great honey <note>likely a reference to a specific alchemical or ritual preparation of incense soot</note>. The term "unfortunate" refers to those who have become hostile. "Without accomplishment" refers to the practitioner. "The other world" refers to other rebirths. The phrase, "endowed with the perfect gift," refers to those with superior devotion to <term>Hevajra</term> <gloss>The Joyful Vajra, a major tantric deity</gloss>. "Only occasionally" means "taught at intervals." "The domain of the path" refers to the time of traveling upon the path. "Shown" means "what has been revealed." By the word "food," the rituals of the <term>elaborate conduct</term> <gloss>active tantric practice with external aids</gloss> and the <term>feast circle</term> <gloss>ganachakra</gloss> are also shown. "Where one has eaten" refers to when one performs the feast circle and the conduct. "All desired goals" refers to the accomplishment of <term>Mahamudra</term> <gloss>The Great Seal, the highest state of realization</gloss>.

To show the specific locations for conduct, the text says "charnel ground" and so forth. "Mountain bird-shelter" means a mountain cave. "And nine" means the number nine has been examined. "Commitments" <note>original: "samaya"</note> refers to <term>go, ku, da, ha, na</term> <gloss>code words for the five meats used in tantric ritual</gloss> and so forth. Regarding the phrase, "having eaten, again," and so forth: "Mothers" <note>original: "mamo"</note> refers to the constituent parts of the eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind; these must be definitively honored with dance, song, and proper offerings.

To show that very point, the text says, "Even if she is a sister," and so forth. By the words "mother" and so forth, the five sense faculties are actually being taught. These are to be satisfied by the five sensory qualities of form, sound, smell, and so on. This is the unsurpassed offering to those goddesses who reside in those sense locations. If one asks, "how could it be anything other than the eyes and so forth?", it is just as it was stated in the <term>Yogini Tantra</term> <gloss>class of tantras focused on feminine energy</gloss> called the <term>Buddhakapala</term> <gloss>The Buddha's Skull</gloss>:

Next, it shall be perfectly explained:
The impure mind must be purified.
The eye is the sister;
The ear is the sister's daughter;
The nose is the mother who gave birth;
Likewise, the tongue is the daughter;
The mind is the wife.
By these five supreme divine substances,
The Great Seal is perfectly bestowed.

Regarding the phrase, "having honored them well"...

The syllable "Ba" is to be experienced continuously without interruption. Regarding the phrase "as a single part" and so forth, "the great skull" refers to the skull of a <term>twice-born</term> <gloss>a member of the higher social classes in Indian tradition, such as a Brahmin</gloss>. "Offer" refers to the beginning of the ritual. "Drink" refers to the subsequent action. The chapter that clarifies the consumption of food also speaks in this manner.

This concludes the commentary on the seventh chapter of the second part of the <term>Yogaratnamala</term> <gloss>The Precious Garland of Yoga</gloss>, which is a difficult points commentary on the <term>Hevajra Tantra</term> <gloss>The Tantra of Hevajra, a major deity in Vajrayana Buddhism</gloss>.

Regarding the phrase "after that" and so forth, "the Great Seal" <note>original: "Mahamudra"</note> is exactly as described previously. Now, concerning the practitioners who perform the ritual with elaborate activity, what is the nature of the partner through whom the Great Seal will be accomplished? Therefore, the text says, "of conventional conduct," meaning according to the conventions of the world. "Through conduct" refers to words of affection and so forth. "Form" refers to color, scent, and such qualities. "Navel of the deer" refers to musk. "Equal" means appearing similar. "Supreme power" refers to the <term>utpala</term> <gloss>blue lotus</gloss>. "Momentary" means occurring occasionally. "Arising" means arising everywhere. "Blood" refers to <term>turuska</term> <gloss>a type of incense or resin</gloss>. "Of that" refers to the body. "Black agarwood" refers to agarwood possessed of the supreme scent. "Charming woman" means one who makes the mind joyful.

Regarding "Reading the profound Dharma," this means reading the <term>Hevajra Tantra</term>. "Those who have become disciplined" refers to the disciples themselves. "Restoration and Purification" <note>original: "Sojong" or "Posadha"</note> refers to the period such as the full moon, lasting from before the sun rises until it has risen. "The bases of training" refers to the eight or fourteen precepts undertaken for as long as one lives; these are characterized by purifying the misdeeds of body, speech, and mind.

"Those who speak for the sake of being free from attachment" refers to the <term>Vaibhashika</term> <gloss>Great Exposition School, one of the four main tenet systems of Indian Buddhism</gloss>. That itself is the <term>Vaibhashika</term> system. Furthermore, that school's traditions include the <term>Hundred Accounts</term> <note>original: "Avadana-shataka"</note> of the Listener <note>original: "Shravaka"</note> vehicle and the <term>Garland of Three Staves</term> and so forth. "The Discourses" <note>original: "Sutras"</note> refers to the discourses that are not extremely profound, such as the <term>One Verse Discourse</term>, the <term>Four Verse Discourse</term>, the <term>Two Verse Incantation</term>, the <term>Six Gates</term>, the <term>Excellent Conduct</term> <note>original: "Bhadracarya"</note>, and the <term>Extensive Play</term> <note>original: "Lalitavistara"</note>.

<meta>continues from previous page: ...the ten stages and so forth.</meta> The term <term>Yogachara</term> <gloss>Practitioner of Yoga</gloss> refers to the teaching that these various appearances are merely the mind. It is taught that when one is deluded regarding the nature of reality, which is not truly existent, things appear as objects; this is described as being like a dream. The term <term>Madhyamaka</term> <gloss>Middle Way</gloss> refers to the fact that all phenomena are without inherent birth.

The phrase "all vehicles of the secret mantra" refers to the five-fold division of <term>Kriya</term> <gloss>Action</gloss>, <term>Charya</term> <gloss>Performance</gloss>, <term>Yoga</term> <gloss>Union</gloss>, <term>Anuttara Yoga</term> <gloss>Unsurpassed Union</gloss>, and <term>Niruttara Yoga</term> <gloss>Absolute Union</gloss>. Regarding the systems of the <term>Vaibhashika</term> <gloss>Great Exposition School</gloss> and others, it is said that one should understand their general treatises only, for their actual substances are beyond measure. The term "having taken up" means to act with devotion. "With devotion" means having devotion for this specific <term>tantra</term> <gloss>lineage text</gloss>.

This concludes the commentary on the eighth chapter of the second section from the <term>Yogaratnamala</term> <gloss>The Precious Garland of Yoga</gloss>, which is a difficult-point commentary on the <term>Hevajra Tantra</term>.

Regarding the phrase "after that" and so forth: <term>Samputa</term> <gloss>Union</gloss> refers to the union of consciousness and the body. "Differentiating" means making a distinction. The phrase "through meditative concentration" refers to what remains. "Siddhi" <gloss>Attainment</gloss> refers here to the attainment of wrathful activities. "Disturbed" means being extremely fierce. "Malevolent" refers to the intent to kill. "Meditation" refers to what was just explained. "That very thing" means that alone. Regarding the word "Buddha," it means that even if one is perfectly protected by the Buddhas and so forth. "Having seen" means having remembered. "In the form of" refers to the forms that will be explained. "Needle" refers to the <term>vajra</term> <gloss>adamantine</gloss> needle. "Possessing the form of fire" means becoming ablaze. "Seed of the fire-consumer" <gloss>Agni</gloss> refers to the intensely blazing syllable <term>Ram</term>. "Having visualized" means having meditated. The phrase "accomplished by reciting" means that the meaning of the words is true until completion. "Secret" refers to that which is not the sphere of experience for sentient beings who lack the fortunate connection. "Supreme" means achieving the desired result without hardship. "Non-conceptual" means without doubt. "Jewel" refers to the precious wish-fulfilling gem. If one asks what that jewel is, the text says "the body," referring to the primordial state.

A.text:
{D1189} In the Indian language: <term>Shri Hevajra Panjika Nama Muktika Avali</term> <gloss>The String of Pearls: A Difficult Points Commentary on the Glorious Hevajra</gloss>. In the Tibetan language: <term>dpal dgyes pa'i rdo rje'i dka' 'grel mu tig phreng ba zhes bya ba</term>. 

I pay homage to the Glorious Vajra Dakini <note>A female buddha representing wisdom and emptiness</note>.

May the dance of the <term>Heruka</term> <gloss>blood-drinker/hero</gloss>, the essence of the essences of the Three Secrets of the Victors <note>The secrets of the Buddha's enlightened body, speech, and mind</note>, protect you.
He whose footsteps shatter the four grounds <note>referring to the directions or levels of the earth</note>, whose intense laughter topples the mountain-holders <note>kings or great mountains</note>;
He who destroys and then revives all beings through the rays of his eyes and the sound of the banner’s bell;
He who possesses the means of showing terrifying rites to utterly pacify those puffed up with pride.

Because it teaches the sutras that follow the standard measures,
And because it is clear and exceedingly beautiful,
This <term>Hevajra</term> Difficult Points Commentary is composed,
Pleasing to the mind like a string of pearls.

The primary word is for those without faith.
It is a place where one strays regarding the unity with the deity.
Because the All-Knowing One is the valid authority,
One does not become all-knowing through mere devotion.

Whether the Victorious One created it or did not,
To say he spoke what he did not, or did speak it—
Toward the Sugata <gloss>One Gone to Bliss</gloss>, the supreme and unfailing guide of beings,
Both of these constitute a similar form of mockery.

The Victorious One spoke of many benefits,
Which people take according to their own intentions.
Likewise, in explaining the meaning in this commentary,
One enters into it according to one’s desire.

If there is no realization, there is no hearing <note>studying the teachings</note>.
If there is no hearing, there is no contemplation.
When both are impaired, there is no yoga <gloss>union/practice</gloss>.
If there is no yoga, there will be no accomplishment.

In this way, may this work snatch away the hearts
Of those who have long been tormented by desire,
Like a string of pearls being threaded
Within this very tantra.

Regarding the words of the introduction, such as "Thus have I heard," some say that because this is a condensed version, it is actually a different tantra. Others say that this second section <term>kalpa</term> was extracted from the Great Tantra, and that it was condensed and placed here exactly as it was, along with the introductory words. Others say that this is a different meaning of the supreme Great Secret. That is correct, for it is improper to express it at the very beginning; it depends on what will be explained later and on the letters themselves. Therefore, one applies the different meaning to the different meaning that is to be explained.

<summary>This page begins the Muktikavali, a commentary on the Hevajra Tantra, opening with a poetic invocation of the deity Heruka and a justification for the commentary's existence. It addresses the philosophical necessity of the teachings and begins to discuss the origins and structure of the tantra's introductory phrases.</summary>
<keywords>Hevajra Tantra, Muktikavali, Heruka, Three Secrets, Yoga, Sugata, String of Pearls, commentary origins</keywords>

B.text:
{D1189} In the language of India: <term>Shri Hevajra Panjika Nama Muktika Avali</term> <gloss>The String of Pearls: A Commentary on the Difficult Points of the Glorious Hevajra</gloss>. In the language of Tibet: <term>Pal Gyepe Dorje Kah-drel Mutik Trengwa</term> <gloss>The String of Pearls: A Commentary on the Difficult Points of the Glorious Hevajra</gloss>.

I bow to the glorious <term>Vajra Dakini</term> <gloss>Diamond Sky-Goer</gloss>.

May you be protected by the dance of <term>Heruka</term> <gloss>The Blood-Drinker/Unconditioned Hero</gloss>, who is the essence of the essences of the Three Secrets of the Victors <note>the secrets of body, speech, and mind of a Buddha</note>. 
By placing his feet, he shatters the four earths. 
By his intense laughter, he topples the mountains. 
With the light of his eyes and the sound of his banners and bells, he destroys all wandering beings and then restores them to life. 
He holds the methods that show terrifying rites to utterly pacify those puffed up with pride.

Because it teaches the <term>Sutras</term> <gloss>Discourses</gloss> that follow the authentic standard, 
And because it is clear and exceptionally beautiful, 
This delightful commentary on the <term>Hevajra</term> <gloss>The Joyous Diamond</gloss> 
Shall be composed like a string of pearls.

The word "principal" is meaningless to those without faith. 
It is a place of straying from being one with the deity. 
Because the Omniscient One <note>the Buddha</note> is the valid authority, 
One does not become omniscient through mere devotion. 
To say the Victor did not do what he did, 
Or to say he spoke what he did not speak, 
Are both equally mocking towards the <term>Sugata</term> <gloss>The One Gone to Bliss</gloss>, the supreme undeceiving guide of beings. 

The Victor spoke of many benefits, 
Which people take according to their own inclinations. 
Likewise, in this commentary, though the meaning is explained, 
One engages with it according to one's own desire. 
Without realization, there is no hearing. 
Without hearing, there is no contemplation. 
If both are impaired, there is no yoga. 
Without yoga, there will be no accomplishment. 
Thus, for those whose hearts have long been scorched by desire, 
Let this string of pearls, threaded within this Tantra, captivate them.

Regarding the introductory words "Thus have I heard" and so forth, some say that because it is an abridgment, it is actually a different Tantra. 
Others say that this "Second Part" was extracted from a Great Tantra <note>referring to the lost original version of the Hevajra Tantra said to consist of 500,000 stanzas</note>, and that it was summarized exactly as it was there and placed here together with the introductory words. 
Others say this has a different, supreme, and great secret meaning. 
That is correct, for it would be improper to state it at the beginning, as it will be explained later and relies upon the written syllables. Therefore, one applies a different meaning to the different meaning that is to be explained...

It is so. Furthermore, the retinue consists of the <term>Bodhisattva</term> <gloss>heroic being of awakening</gloss> <term>Vajragarbha</term> <gloss>Vajra Essence</gloss> and others, the <term>Locanā</term> and others, and the <term>Vajrayoginī</term> <gloss>diamond female practitioners</gloss> such as <term>Gaurī</term> and others. As for the phrase "there," it means while residing there. Regarding the phrase "he spoke," if one asks for whose benefit he spoke, it was for the benefit of those beings who were tormented by the desire to hear the teachings. 

If one asks what he spoke, it begins with the phrase "of all the <term>Tathāgatas</term> <gloss>Thus Gone Ones</gloss>." A <term>Tathāgata</term> is one who has gone as far as there is to travel; they have abandoned all obscurations along with their habitual tendencies. Alternatively, the word "gone" <note>original: "gatis"</note> has the meaning of "realization." Because they realize reality exactly as it is, as suchness, these are called <term>Tathāgatas</term>. They perfectly realize all that is to be known in every possible way. 

Alternatively, the syllables may be translated in the present tense: because he speaks exactly as things are to be demonstrated, he is a <term>Tathāgata</term>. He perfectly teaches the genuine <term>Dharma</term> <gloss>Buddha's teaching</gloss> in accordance with the intentions, dispositions, and needs of those to be trained, as well as the specific time. He is all of those things, and he is also the <term>Tathāgata</term>. 

The <term>Vajradhara</term> <gloss>Vajra Holder</gloss> is the very essence of their body, speech, and mind. The "heart" or "essence" refers to the most excellent. The term "Venerable" <note>original: "Bhagavan"</note> refers to the supreme deity. The essence of the body, speech, and mind of all the deities of secret mantra, who are the nature of non-conceptual primordial wisdom, is itself that which is most difficult to trust or comprehend. Their "great secret" is that which is even more secret than the secret itself. Because he is endowed with great intensity and is called <term>Hevajra</term> <gloss>Vajra of Joy</gloss>, possessing the supreme intensity and great passion of body, speech, and mind, he is therefore the secret beyond the secret. The intention is that even faith in this is extremely difficult to find. 

The word "this" carries the meaning of "in this manner." For the retinue tormented by the desire to hear, three thoughts arise. The first thought is: "If this is indeed the secret beyond the secret, when and what kind of person would be fortunate enough to receive it? This must be explained." The second thought is: "Is it the established conclusion that there is no supreme being other than the <term>Vajradhara</term>?" Of that itself...

The second <note>point of inquiry</note> is: "Is this the essence, or is there another even more supreme than this, called Body, Speech, and Mind?" The third point is: "What is the name of this venerable one?" In order to clarify these concepts, he said, "How wonderful!" <note>original: "Emaho"</note> and so forth. At the end of this phrase, one should take the word "this" from the previous sentence and apply it to understand its own meaning. "This too" means "something like this." If the word "this" is missing in some versions, one should still understand it to be present through the context.

"How wonderful! <term>Vajragarbha</term> <gloss>Adamantine Essence</gloss>" means that all Bodhisattvas are the <term>Tathagatagarbha</term> <gloss>Essence of the One Thus Gone</gloss> and belong to the <term>Tathagata-gotra</term> <gloss>Buddha Family</gloss>. 

The five <term>Tathagata</term> families are ignorance, hatred, pride, desire, and jealousy. In that context, that which is characterized by hatred is <term>Vajragarbha</term>. The name of this Bodhisattva accords with its meaning. It is difficult to find a Bodhisattva lineage such as this. Because of this, he called out in amazement, saying, "How wonderful!"

"That essence, the Bodhisattva, the Great Being, excellent, excellent!" indicates that the intention to perform the welfare of others through methods such as supreme wrath is itself Great Compassion. Through that very compassion, the continuous attainment of various purposes at all times is Great Awakening. One who possesses such a perfect intention is a Great Bodhisattva. One who has such an intention to benefit others and an intention to benefit oneself is the supreme among beings. For this reason, he said "excellent" twice.

"Listen!" is the instruction to apply oneself to hearing. This indicates that a noble person with such a lineage and such an intention is one who possesses the required fortune. If one asks how this lineage is known, it is through the specific signs of faith and desire for its qualities. As stated in the <term>Lankavatara Sutra</term>: 

By smoke, fire is known;
By water-fowl, water is <unclear>known</unclear>

<summary>This page explains the symbolic and technical meaning of the Bodhisattva Vajragarbha and the five Buddha families, defining Great Compassion as the intent to benefit others through various means.</summary>
<keywords>Vajragarbha, Tathagatagarbha, five families, Buddha lineage, Great Compassion, Lankavatara Sutra</keywords>

B.text:
Is this essence, or is it another more supreme one called Body, Speech, and Mind? This is the second <note>point of doubt or inquiry</note>. What is the name of this Venerable One? This is the third. To clarify these conceptions, the text says: "How wonderful!" <note>original: "E ma ho"</note> and so forth.

At the end of this phrase, one should take the word "this" from the previous sentence and apply it to understand its own meaning. "This too" means "even such as this." If the word "this" is absent in some versions, one should still understand the meaning in that way.

The phrase "How wonderful, Vajra Essence!" <note>original: "E ma ho rdo rje sྙing po"</note> means that all Bodhisattvas are the <term>Tathagatagarbha</term> <gloss>Essence of the One Gone to Bliss</gloss> and the <term>Tathagata-gotra</term> <gloss>Buddha Family or lineage</gloss>.

The five Buddha families are ignorance, hatred, pride, desire, and jealousy. In this context, that which is characterized by hatred is the <term>Vajra-garbha</term> <gloss>Vajra Essence</gloss>. The name of this Bodhisattva accords with its meaning. It is difficult to find a Bodhisattva lineage such as this. Because of the wonder felt at this, the text calls out: "How wonderful!"

Regarding the phrase "That Essence, Bodhisattva, Great Hero <note>original: "Mahasattva"</note>, excellent, excellent!": the intention to accomplish the benefit of others through methods such as supreme wrath is itself Great Compassion. Through that, the Awakening that accomplishes various purposes without a fixed time is Great Awakening. One who truly contemplates this is a Great Heroic Bodhisattva. One who possesses such an intention to benefit others and an intention to benefit themselves is the supreme of beings. For that reason, the word "excellent" is repeated twice.

The command "Listen!" is the engagement in hearing. This demonstrates that a holy being with such a lineage and such an intention is one who possesses the fortunate karmic connection. How is this lineage to be known? It is known through the specific signs of faith and desire for its qualities. As stated in the *Noble Descent into Lanka Sutra* <note>original: "Arya-Lankavatara-sutra"</note>:

By smoke, one knows there is fire;
By the water-crane, one knows there is water.

"Consciousness" refers to the master’s expertise in all rituals. "The Deities" refers to the glorious Heruka with his retinue, or Nairatmya <gloss>She who is Without Self</gloss>. "How they arise" means how they are generated appropriately. "The other" refers to the gazes, summoning, and so forth that were mentioned. "Heruka" is the Fruitional Hevajra. "Generation" is the attainment of that state. Its cause is the "Method Tantra." Why is this mentioned first? Because this is most excellent due to the many methods of the generation stage, such as the deities and so forth.

Now, in this Great Vehicle <term>Mahayana</term>, all phenomena are shown to be the body through "mere cognition" <term>vijnaptimatra</term>. As stated in the noble *Ten Stages Sutra*: "This triple world is mind only." The nature of that cognition is clarity; if its nature were not clarity, it would not become clear, as that would be contradictory. Because blue, yellow, and so forth appear clearly, there are no external objects outside of consciousness. At that time, what is it like? It is the mind itself, established by similar karmic imprints—the forms, appearances, and experiences that are the nature of consciousness—arising in various aspects, just like a dream. 

As stated in the noble *Lankavatara Sutra*:
Just as children imagine it,
External objects do not exist.
The mind, stirred by habitual tendencies,
Appears as objects.

"Stirred" means thoroughly disturbed. Furthermore, external objects like blue and so forth do not exist because they are free from being either one or many. They are not "one" because they appear separately through the division of parts. Nor are they "many atoms," because the concept of atoms is illogical. If one says they have parts, how could they be "atoms" <gloss>the smallest indivisible units</gloss>? If they have no parts, then because all atoms would merge entirely through contact, they would occupy the same space; thus elephants, mountains, oceans, and the earth would all be the size of a single atom.

B.text:
Consciousness <note>Tibetan: rnam shes</note> refers to being skilled in all the activities of the master. The phrase the deities <note>Tibetan: lha rnams</note> refers to the glorious Heruka together with his retinue, or alternatively, to Nairatmya <note>the female personification of egolessness</note>. The phrase how they arise <note>Tibetan: ji ltar 'byung ba</note> means how they are generated in a suitable manner. The phrase the other <note>Tibetan: cig shos</note> refers to the gazes, the rites of summoning, and so forth as they have been explained. Heruka is the result, Hevajra. Generation <note>Tibetan: bskyed pa</note> means attaining his level. Its cause is the meaning of the Method Tantra <note>Tibetan: thabs kyi rgyud</note>. Why is this mentioned first? Because this method of the generation stage <note>Tibetan: bskyed pa'i rim pa</note> through the forms of deities and so forth is the most excellent.

Furthermore, in this Great Vehicle, all phenomena are shown to be contained within consciousness alone. The Noble Ten Bhumis Scripture <note>Sanskrit: Dashabhumika Sutra</note> says: Thus, this triple world is mind only. The nature of that consciousness is clarity. If it were not of this nature, it would not be clear, as that would be a contradiction. Because blue, yellow, and so forth appear clearly, there are no external objects existing outside of consciousness.

What is the situation then? It is the mind itself, established by similar patterns of conceptual thought, which arises in various forms such as aspect, appearance, and experience, just like a dream. The Noble Descent into Lanka Scripture <note>Sanskrit: Lankavatara Sutra</note> says:

External objects do not exist
In the way the foolish imagine them.
The mind, stirred up by latent tendencies <note>Sanskrit: vasana</note>,
Appears as external objects.

Stirred up means afflicted. Furthermore, external objects like blue and so forth do not exist because they lack the nature of being either one or many. They are not one because they appear as distinct parts. They are also not many atoms because the concept of atoms is illogical. If an atom has parts, how can it be a minute atom? If it has no parts, then when atoms join together with their entire essence, they would be inseparable and occupy the same space. Thus, elephants, mountains, oceans, and the entire mass of the earth would be reduced to the size of a single minute atom.

<summary>This page explains the generation stage of the Heruka deity and provides a philosophical defense of the Mind Only view. It argues that external objects are mental projections and uses the logical refutation of atoms to prove that only consciousness exists.</summary>
<keywords>Heruka, Hevajra, generation stage, Mind Only, Yogacara, consciousness, Dashabhumika Sutra, Lankavatara Sutra, refutation of atoms</keywords>

Regarding that thought, it is said: "The bondage of entities," and so forth. Here, the word "entities" refers to the first five perfections, for they are primary in acting as the support and in the attainment. The bondage of entities itself is the act of supporting. Those who are liberated while bound by that remain for the benefit of all beings through the power of those [perfections], in the continuity of the Three Bodies, until the end of space. 

Thoroughly knowing those entities is the knowledge of the Ultimate, which is the Perfection of Wisdom itself. By that one is liberated; by that one abandons all obscurations of habitual tendencies, and all afflictive phenomena, including their seeds, are completely exhausted. This is Nirvana, specifically the "Non-abiding Nirvana," for one abides in neither cyclic existence nor [solitary] peace. 

The summary is given: "The entity," and so forth. "Entity" refers to the virtue arising from the five perfections. "Should be meditated upon" means it should be produced with diligence in the continuity of one's own mind, and through the power of meditation, one should be endowed with that nature. "By thoroughly knowing non-entities" means by the Wisdom Paramita that thoroughly knows the non-existence of the nature of grasped and grasper. If one does not treat the entity as an entity, one is liberated but falls into the Enlightenment of a Hearer. If one does not thoroughly know it, one remains in cyclic existence. Both are confused. 

A Bodhisattva endowed with Wisdom does both; hence he is addressed as "Wise One." This summarizes and establishes what is to be done in the Great Vehicle. Since the Great Vehicle is also contained within the Mantrayana <gloss>Secret Mantra Vehicle</gloss>, Hevajra is further shown. As it is said: "Thus," and so forth. By mentioning "Heruka," the principal figure, his signs, seats, celestial palaces, and retinue are also included, just as one says, "The King is coming."

B.text:
Thinking about this, the author stated: "The bondage of things" <note>original: "dngos po'i 'ching ba"</note> and so forth. Here, the term "things" refers to the five perfections <note>the perfections of generosity, discipline, patience, diligence, and concentration</note>, because these are the primary factors for remaining in the world and for attainment. The bondage of things itself is that which causes one to remain. Those who are liberated through being bound by these perfections remain for the benefit of all beings throughout the continuum of the three bodies <term>trikaya</term> <gloss>the three dimensions of a Buddha: the truth, enjoyment, and emanation bodies</gloss> until the very limits of space.

Thoroughly knowing the nature of these things is the knowledge of the ultimate truth, which is the perfection of wisdom <term>prajnaparamita</term> <gloss>transcendent wisdom</gloss> itself. Being liberated by this, one abandons all obscurations of habitual tendencies; this means completely exhausting all afflicted phenomena along with their seeds. This state is nirvana, specifically described as non-abiding nirvana <term>apratisthita-nirvana</term> <gloss>a state where a Buddha stays neither in the cycle of suffering nor in a state of solitary peace</gloss>, because one abides neither in cyclic existence nor in personal liberation.

Regarding the summary provided in the text starting with "things" and so forth: "things" refers to the virtue arising from the five perfections. "Should be meditated upon" means one should exert effort to generate these in the continuum of one's own mind and become endowed with them through the power of meditation.

"By thoroughly knowing the absence of things" means through the perfection of wisdom which thoroughly understands that things lack an inherent nature of subject and object. If one does not treat things as things <note>referring to engaging in the perfections</note>, one is liberated but falls into the enlightenment of a Hearer <term>shravaka</term> <gloss>one who seeks only personal liberation</gloss>. Yet, if one does not thoroughly know their nature, one remains in cyclic existence. Both paths are characterized by delusion.

The Bodhisattva who possesses wisdom does both <note>remains in the world through the perfections while knowing their empty nature</note>. For that reason, they are addressed as "The Wise One." This summarizes the conduct of the Great Vehicle <term>Mahayana</term> and establishes its system. Because the Great Vehicle is also contained within the Way of Secret Mantra, the <term>Hevajra</term> <gloss>the "Joyful Vajra" tantra</gloss> is taught as the superior method. Thus it says, "In that way" and so forth. By mentioning the principal figure "Heruka" <gloss>a wrathful semi-nude male deity representing enlightened consciousness</gloss>, one also includes his attributes, his seat, and the celestial palace, just as one says "The King approaches" <note>implying his whole retinue and court are included in the statement</note>.

<summary>This page explains how a Bodhisattva uses the first five perfections to remain in the world for others while using the sixth perfection, wisdom, to avoid being trapped by worldly existence. It defines non-abiding nirvana as the balance between these two states and links this Mahayana path to the Hevajra Tantra.</summary>
<keywords>perfections, paramitas, non-abiding nirvana, Bodhisattva, Hevajra, Heruka, emptiness, Mahayana</keywords>

House-Mother <term>Grhadharma</term>, Fierce One <term>Candika</term>, and Demon-Subduer <term>Marasundari</term>—these three are the Sky-Walker <term>Khecari</term>.

Therefore, all channels are included within the fifteen yoginis. This will also be explained in the Chapter on the Collection of All Mantras and Seals. In the Chapter on the Families, it is said:
"The nature of the sixteen doubled <note>thirty-two</note> is taught.
For each yogini,
Two channels are assigned in order.
Lalana, Rasana,
And Avadhuti are Nairatmya."
And:
"The mind of enlightenment becomes the moon,
Possessing fifteen parts.
The nature of the vowels <term>ali</term> is Great Bliss;
The yoginis are its parts."

Here, just as the first Nairatmya has three channels, the final yogini Khecari also has three channels; this is the implied meaning. Otherwise, the claim that two channels are included for each yogini would not hold, especially since it is said that "thirty-two [channels] of the mind of enlightenment flow."

In the Yogini Tantras, the mind of enlightenment is divided into thirty-two, and these abide in the Wheel of Great Bliss. Furthermore, from each of the thirty-two channels, the mind of enlightenment flows from the Wheel of Great Bliss. Thus, we shall explain where their primary locations and flows are.

The divisions of these yogini-natures should be distinguished according to the divisions of the tantras, as all causes are not identical. The minor channels that circulate everywhere and follow one another should be understood according to how their locations and functions are taught.

Also, from the *Union of the Kiss* and the *Vajradaka*:

Is the channel endowed with the Enjoyment Body <term>sambhogakaya</term>.
Resting in the center of the navel,
Looking downward, the intoxicated one

<summary>This page continues the mapping of subtle body channels to the yoginis of the Hevajra mandala, specifically identifying Lalana, Rasana, and Avadhuti. it discusses the flow of white and red drops (semen and blood) from the palate to the navel and the symbolic numbering of thirty-two channels.</summary>

Therefore, all the <term>nadis</term> <gloss>subtle energy channels</gloss> are condensed within these fifteen <term>yoginis</term>. 

This is also explained in the chapter on the summary of all mantras and mudras. Regarding the channels from the chapter on the Buddha-families:
The nature of sixteen multiplied by two is taught.
Each of the <term>yoginis</term>

There are <term>Lalana</term>, <term>Rasana</term>,

The <term>bodhichitta</term> <gloss>enlightened essence/semen</gloss> becomes the Moon,

According to the <term>Yogini-tantras</term>, the <term>bodhichitta</term> is divided into thirty-two parts, which reside in the <term>Chakra of Great Bliss</term> <gloss>located at the crown of the head</gloss>. From these thirty-two individual channels, the <term>bodhichitta</term> flows out from the <term>Chakra of Great Bliss</term>. Therefore, I shall explain the specific locations where they primarily reside and how they flow. The distinctions between these natures of the yoginis should be differentiated according to the specific Tantras, as not all causes are identical. One should understand how the minor branch channels circulate everywhere and interconnect based on the explanations of their locations and functions.

From the <term>Samputa Tantra</term> <gloss>The Tantra of the Union</gloss>:
In the center of the birth-place <gloss>the secret center</gloss> are two channels,

Know that the white seed <gloss>semen</gloss> flows from the left,
and the blood <gloss>ovum/menstrual fluid</gloss> flows from the right.

Furthermore, it is taught in the <term>Samputa</term> and the <term>Vajradaka Tantra</term>:
Starting from the palate on the left side,
the channel is endowed with the <term>Sambhogakaya</term> <gloss>Enjoyment Body</gloss>.
Resting in the center of the navel,
looking downward, it is intoxicated...

<summary>This page explains the correlation between fifteen yoginis and the thirty-two subtle channels of the body, detailing how the enlightened essence flows from the crown chakra through these channels. It cites the Samputa Tantra to describe the binary nature of the channels in relation to the male and female essences.</summary>

In what is widely known as the 'short' one,
It abides at the navel in the form of A.
Endowed with two hooks <note>the vowel markers</note>,
The long HUM abides in both.
Endowed with three hooks,
In the throat it is the nature of OM.
With the sound <term>nada</term> and the drop <term>bindu</term>,
In the forehead is the indestructible HAM,
The form of glorious Vajrasattva,
Who plays just as he pleases.
In the four directions of the center,
Upon the four petals,
With the nature of a burning lamp,
Are the channels of the four great elements."

If one asks how these three tantras teach the channels consistently: the meaning is that what is not taught here is established elsewhere, and thus it is intended here as well. Lalana and Rasana begin from the throat and extend to the inner boundary of the navel; the channels on the left and right sides are called Moon and Sun. The two channels of the birth-place below the navel are those very same Lalana and Rasana. The five channels of the heart are Three-Entrants, Desire-Possessor, House-Mother, Fierce One, and Demon-Subduer.

If one asks why the *Union of the Kiss* mentions one hundred and twenty: that is the division of the four wheels. Here, the thirty-two supreme channels of the nature of the mind of enlightenment are discussed. Thus, there is no contradiction at all. There,

Here, the three primary channels are the yogini Nairatmya. The final three—House-Mother and so forth—are Khecari. The remaining thirteen pairs of channels are the yoginis Gauri and the rest.

A.text: Above that, one views the garland of thirty-four consonants from KA onwards in the same way and meditates on it becoming a sun disk. This becoming a sun from the total transformation of KALI is the "sun through KALI," which is the Wisdom of Equality. "The seed abiding in the center" means abiding in the center of the sun; it is the blue vajra born from the seed abiding there on top of the center of the sun. This is the meaning of "The seed abides in the center of the navel." That very mind which has become the form of the seed <term>HUM</term> is called the "Being" <term>sattva</term>; that which is born as the seed is called Vajrasattva. If one asks what it is like, it possesses the nature of supreme joy, which is the nature of Means and Wisdom. Arising from the union of the ALI-moon and the KALI-sun, it has three divisions of the nature of Great Bliss: the preliminary union, the actual state, and the conclusion. This is the Wisdom of Discriminating Awareness. "Projecting outwards" means from that very seed of one's own. If one asks what is projected, it is "one's own similar body," like the body of Hevajra. All the deities of the mantra are summarized as the bodies of the fifteen yoginis, blue in color and possessing a wrathful expression, which become the means to tame all beings, adorning and covering the sphere of the sky. "Should be gathered into the heart" means all those bodies of the deities should be gathered and dissolved into that very seed. All these becoming one with the seed of one's own mantra is the Wisdom of All-Accomplishing Action. Then, "The yogi becomes possessed of the nature of anger" means that the moon, sun, vajra, and seed having totally transformed, the body of Hevajra appears, possessed of the colors, attire, expressions, and signs that will be described. These are the Wisdom of the Perfectly Pure Sphere of Phenomena <term>dharmadhatu-vishuddha-jnana</term>, which is the finding of Great Awakening in the essence of the supreme transformation of the basis. Thus, the manifest awakening by the five wisdoms such as the Mirror-like is the "manifest awakening through five aspects." Know this. Above that, one should observe the garland of the thirty-four consonants starting with <term>Ka</term> <gloss>the Sanskrit alphabet consonants</gloss> in the same manner and meditate on them as having become the solar disk. This process of the <term>Kali</term> <gloss>consonants</gloss> fully transforming into the sun is the Sun of the <term>Kali</term>; it is the Wisdom of Equality.

The phrase "the seed syllable residing in the center" means residing specifically in the center of the sun. On top of the center of the sun, a blue ritual vajra is born from the seed syllable and remains there. This is the meaning of "the seed syllable resides in the center of the navel."

That very seed syllable, having transformed into the form of the syllable <term>Hum</term>, is called the Being. This means that which is born as the seed syllable is itself explained as <term>Vajrasattva</term> <gloss>Vajra Being</gloss>. If one asks what his nature is: he possesses the nature of supreme bliss, which is the nature of Method and Wisdom.

The union of the <term>Ali</term> <gloss>vowels</gloss> as the moon and the <term>Kali</term> <gloss>consonants</gloss> as the sun produces the nature of Great Bliss, which is divided into three parts: the union, the actual manifestation, and the conclusion. This is the Wisdom of Discernment.

The term "emanating" refers to emanating from that very seed syllable of one's own. If one asks what is emanated, it is "likenesses of one's own body," meaning bodies like that of <term>Hevajra</term>. These are the forms of the fifteen <term>yoginis</term> <gloss>female tantric deities</gloss>, which condense all the deities of the mantra. They are blue in color, possessing a wrathful expression, and serve as the method to subdue all beings, adorning and filling the sphere of the sky.

"Gathering into the heart" means that all those forms of the deities should be gathered and dissolved back into that very seed syllable. All of these becoming one within the seed syllable of one's own mantra is the All-Accomplishing Wisdom.

Then, the phrase "the practitioner becomes the embodiment of hatred" <note>Hatred is the transformation of the vajra family in this context.</note> refers to the complete transformation of the moon, the sun, the vajra, and the seed syllable. One then possesses the color, ornaments, expression, and marks of the body of <term>Hevajra</term> as they will be described. These are the Wisdom of the Dharmadhatu <gloss>Sphere of Reality</gloss>, which is perfectly pure. This is the attainment of Great Enlightenment as the essence of the supreme transformation of the foundation.

In this way, becoming enlightened through the five wisdoms, such as the Mirror-like Wisdom and the others, is called the Enlightenment through the Five Aspects. This will be explained in the eighth chapter: "The moon possesses the Mirror-like Wisdom; the Seven-Horsed One <gloss>the sun</gloss> is Equality; the deity's own..."

A.text:
and conduct are the ritual; the ritual of method and wisdom. "Should be worshipped by those desiring that reality" means for the sake of perfectly knowing reality. "With effort" means secretly with diligence. That very effort is stated: "In such a way that one does not become known," and so forth. "Knowing" means being investigated and known by those with the power of knowing other than oneself, or the falling away from secret speech by one's own pride, showing off, or anger, or by an attendant speaking the secret to others. The unseen faults, such as falling into hell if one does not keep the secret, are well known. The seen faults are also stated: "If not kept secret" and so forth. "Snakes and so forth" should be connected to "causes suffering," meaning by snakes and tigers and so forth. "Those who move on the ground" refers to humans, flesh-eaters <note>pishachas</note>, and so forth who inflict punishment. "Mudra" <note>Seal</note> refers to that which symbolizes the families of these, such as the <term>vajra</term> and <term>padma</term> <gloss>lotus</gloss>. "Gone to Suchness" <note>Tathagata</note> means proceeding to the single taste of suchness which is completely pure, thus abiding in the <term>Dharmakaya</term> <gloss>Truth Body</gloss>. "Possessing the Glorious Knowledge" is the Sovereign of all Buddha-phenomena; it is not for Listeners <note>Shravakas</note> and so forth. "Come" <note>Gata</note> means from that very suchness; having come from that is for the sake of the <term>Sambhogakaya</term> <gloss>Enjoyment Body</gloss> and for performing the benefit of beings through the <term>Nirmanakaya</term> <gloss>Emanation Body</gloss>, which are concordant causes of it. Thus, by the word <term>Tathagata</term>, it is made into a single remainder, according to the etymological explanation where a letter is elided, as the "ta" of <term>Tathagata</term> is not visible. Thus, for a moment, all Tathagatas are the five families of those primordial wisdoms, such as the mirror-like and so forth. If one asks: "If all Buddhas possess the five wisdoms, how are they divided by family distinctions?" The family divisions are each of the mirror-like and so forth being similar, and many being similar, making six with the family of the Being <note>Sattva</note>; the families of Bodhisattvas are established from beginningless time. That very point is stated: "The families are explained as sixfold." "Condensed, they are fivefold" is because the sixth, having many similarities, is condensed as it is particularly powerful.

And conduct is the ritual; it is the ritual of method and wisdom. The phrase "it should be offered through the desire for reality" means it is done for the purpose of perfectly realizing suchness. "With effort" means protecting the secret with diligence. That very effort is described as: "in a way that it does not become known."

"To be known" refers to being investigated by those with the power to know things other than themselves, or to the failure of the secret due to oneself or a confidant speaking of it to others out of pride, showing off, or anger, or through a servant. If the secret is not kept, the unseen faults, such as falling into hell and so forth, are extremely well known. The visible faults are also described by the phrase "if not kept secret" and so on. The phrase "snakes and so forth" should be connected to "causing suffering," meaning suffering caused by snakes, tigers, and such. "Those who move on the earth" refers to humans, <term>pishachas</term> <gloss>flesh-eating spirits</gloss>, and others who inflict punishment.

Regarding the term <term>mudra</term> <gloss>seal or hand gesture</gloss>: it is that which symbolizes these families such as the <term>vajra</term> <gloss>diamond-bolt</gloss> and the <term>padma</term> <gloss>lotus</gloss>. Regarding "He who has gone to suchness" <note>original: "Tathagata"</note>: it is to have gone into a single taste within the utterly pure suchness; it is to abide in the <term>dharmakaya</term> <gloss>truth body</gloss>. "Possessing glorious knowledge" means being the sovereign of the qualities of all Buddhas, which the <term>shravakas</term> <gloss>pious listeners</gloss> and others are not.

"Come forth" means from that very suchness. Coming forth from that is for the sake of the welfare of beings through the <term>sambhogakaya</term> <gloss>enjoyment body</gloss> and <term>nirmanakaya</term> <gloss>emanation body</gloss>, which are the natural results of that suchness. In this way, the term <term>Tathagata</term> captures this as a single entity, following the etymological explanation where letters are dropped, such as the hidden "ta" in <term>Tathagata</term>.

In that regard, all <term>Tathagatas</term> consist of the five families of those original wisdoms, such as the mirror-like wisdom and the rest. If all Buddhas possess the five wisdoms, how are they divided into families? The division of families is based on each wisdom like the mirror-like wisdom being similar in part or similar in many parts. Together with the <term>Sattva</term> <gloss>Heroic Being</gloss> family, there are six. Since they are established from beginningless time, these are the families of the <term>Bodhisattvas</term>. As it is said: "The families are explained as being of six types." "When condensed, there are five types" refers to...

primordial wisdom, which is the nature of great bliss, is without elaboration because all marks of delusion have subsided. This very perfect primordial wisdom exhausts the afflictions along with their seeds; it is the <term>Dharmakaya</term> which is the unconditioned sphere, free from elaboration, having abandoned the conceptualizations that appear as environment, body, and enjoyments. These three are pure like space, infinite, and the Truth Body without elaboration; such is the meaning. In that nature, as its very essence, that ultimate exists; therefore, the intention is to directly realize its nature. In that way, that very thing is <term>Vairocana</term> <gloss>The Illuminator</gloss>, by appearing as mere clarity. That very thing is <term>Akshobhya</term> <gloss>The Unshakable</gloss>, by its very non-appearance. That very thing is <term>Amoghasiddhi</term> <gloss>Unfailing Accomplishment</gloss>, by performing various purposes. That very thing is <term>Ratnasambhava</term> <gloss>Jewel-Born</gloss>, by obtaining all Buddha-phenomena. That very thing is <term>Arolik</term> <note>Amitabha's family</note>, by perfectly practicing the identity of those. Thus, that very nature of the five wisdoms is the "Being of Heroic Mind" <term>Sattva</term>, which means <term>Vajrasattva</term>. Regarding "Brahma" and so forth: that very thing is spoken of as Brahma and so forth. If one wonders how, it is stated: "Brahma..." and so forth. That which is the very nature of realizing complete purity, by that very fact, this is a Buddha, and thus supreme Brahma; therefore, "Brahma is Nirvana," which is the very nature of liberation. Nirvana, liberation, peace, and Brahma are synonyms. "Entering" means entering as its very identity. Where? Into the profoundly deep <term>Dharmakaya</term>. "By being always perfectly virtuous" is because it is always virtuous and supremely virtuous. Regarding "All..." and so forth: because this very thing cognizes the <term>dharmadhatu</term> as the identity of all, by abiding in that, it is "All." "Supreme Bliss" is by the very showing of the supreme unconditioned bliss.
