B.text:
The nature of the <term>jnana</term> <gloss>wisdom</gloss> of great bliss is without conceptual elaboration, because all marks of delusion have subsided. This very authentic wisdom exhausts the afflictions along with their seeds. The stainless realm, which abandons the conceptualizations appearing as environment, body, and enjoyments, is also without conceptual elaboration. These three are the purified, space-like, infinite, and elaboration-free <term>dharmakaya</term> <gloss>truth body of a Buddha</gloss>. That ultimate truth exists as that very nature and essence. Therefore, the intention is to make that very nature manifest.

In that regard, that very essence is <term>Vairocana</term> <gloss>the Illuminator</gloss> by appearing as mere clarity. That same essence is <term>Akshobhya</term> <gloss>the Unshakeable</gloss> by the fact of non-appearance itself. That same essence is <term>Amoghasiddhi</term> <gloss>Unfailing Success</gloss> because it performs diverse purposes. That same essence is <term>Ratnasambhava</term> <gloss>the Jewel-Born</gloss> because all the qualities of a Buddha are obtained through it. That same essence is <term>Arolik</term> <note>a seed syllable associated with Amitabha and the Lotus family</note> because it perfectly practices the self-nature of these. Thus, the nature of the five wisdoms is the <term>sattva</term> <gloss>spiritual hero/being</gloss>, which is the meaning of the name <term>Vajrasattva</term> <gloss>Diamond Being</gloss>.

Regarding the passage beginning with "Brahma" and so forth: that very essence is described as Brahma and the rest. To explain why this is thought to be so, the text says: "He is called Brahma," and so on. Since that very nature of realizing perfect purity is the Buddha, he is the supreme Brahma. Thus, the phrase "Brahma is <term>nirvana</term> <gloss>extinction of suffering</gloss>" means the very nature of liberation. "Nirvana," "liberation," "peace," and "Brahma" are synonyms.

The term "entering" refers to entering into the identity of that. Into what? Into the profoundly deep <term>dharmakaya</term>. The phrase "always perfectly virtuous" is used because it is eternally virtuous and supremely virtuous. Regarding the passage beginning with "all": because it abides as that which makes known the <term>dharmadhatu</term> <gloss>sphere of reality</gloss> as the identity of all things, it is therefore called "all." "Supreme bliss" refers to the demonstration of the highest stainless bliss. The phrase "killed by the realization of bliss" <note>an idiomatic or esoteric reference to the destruction of ignorance through bliss</note> means realizing that very unsurpassable bliss. One who does not know that is like one who is asleep. Brahma...

<summary>This page explains the nature of the Dharmakaya as the integration of five wisdoms personified by the Five Buddha Families and Vajrasattva. It equates the realization of ultimate reality with the state of Brahma, defining it as synonymous with nirvana, liberation, and supreme bliss.</summary>
<keywords>Jnana, Dharmakaya, Five Buddhas, Vajrasattva, Nirvana, Brahma, Dharmadhatu, Supreme Bliss</keywords>

A.text:
Brahma and so forth that have been shown, after explaining these, others are also spoken: "Body..." and so forth. That itself is the deity, that which arises from the body; such is the meaning. <term>Dehasambhava</term> means "arising from the body"; in the first word the "ha" is made invisible, and in the second the "sam-bha" is made invisible; it is the deity of that which arises from the body. Because this is shown to be easily found, it is "easily found" as it arises from the body. "In that Buddha" means in Buddhahood itself. "All the qualities of sovereignty and so forth" refers to Brahma. As it was said: "Sovereignty and good form, glory and fame and primordial wisdom, and possessing the excellence of diligence; these six are explained as *Bhaga* <gloss>Blessed/Fortune</gloss>." In this context, because there is "destruction" <note>bhag-</note> <gloss>of maras</gloss>, the term is applied. Having spoken of the ultimate truth, again for the sake of completely filling the accumulations very quickly through the conventional truth, it is said: "Ma" and so forth. By the words "Ma" and so forth, only Wisdom <note>Prajña</note> is spoken of, not necessarily an external distinction. This is the condensed meaning. "Producing the world" refers to the world of Nobles <note>Aryas</note>. It is not others, for they lack the mind of realization. "Dividing" refers to the various objects of knowledge. "Washerwoman" and so forth are the indicators. "By washing" and so forth is the explanation. "Of sentient beings" refers to consciousness. "Qualities" refers to supreme bliss. "Moving" is because of entering quickly into the objects of knowledge. "Expression is the recitation" means the expressions arising from the pride of Hevajra are the recitation of the essence and the mantra. This is the very condensed summary. "Drawn by the feet" means the drawing of foot-prints on dust, mud, water, and so forth is the "mandala"; this is the very condensed summary. "Treading" means being trodden upon by Hevajra or being the support of Hevajra; for the verbal root of "mother" <term>ma-</term>

<summary>This page explains the etymology of "Bhagavan" through its six qualities and links the conventional practice of mudras and mandalas to the internal realization of wisdom. It concludes with a condensed explanation of tantric recitation and mandala creation as expressions of the deity's pride.</summary>
<keywords>Dehasambhava, Bhaga, Bhagavan, conventional truth, wisdom, mantra recitation, mandala, sentient beings</keywords>

B.text:
Having explained the activities and other teachings, he states further: Regarding the phrase "the body" and so forth, the deity itself is produced from the body; this is the meaning. The term <term>dehasambhava</term> <gloss>arising from the body</gloss> means it originates from the body. In the previous syllable, the letter "ha" is made unmanifest, and in the following "sambha," it is also made unmanifest, meaning the deity itself arises from the body. Because this shows that it is easily found, its arising from the body makes it easily obtained. The phrase "to that Buddha" means "to Buddhahood itself." The phrase "all qualities such as lordship" refers to Brahma. As it is said:

Lordship and good form,
Glory, fame, and wisdom,
And the perfection of diligence:
These six are called "blessed."

Thus it was said. In this context, the words are arranged to show that "one who possesses these qualities is Blessed" <note>original: bhagavan</note>. Having explained the ultimate truth, he speaks again regarding the relative truth in order to complete the accumulations very quickly: "The Mother" and so forth. By the word "Mother" and similar terms, only wisdom is expressed; it certainly does not refer to external distinctions. This is the summarized meaning. The phrase "generating the world" refers to the world of the noble ones. It is no other, because there is no mind of realization otherwise. "Distinguishing" refers to the various objects of knowledge. Terms such as "the washerwoman" are the basic teachings. The explanation is given through terms like "washing." The word "sentient beings" refers to consciousness. "Qualities" refers to supreme bliss. "Moving" refers to the rapid engagement with objects of knowledge. The phrase "recitation is that which expresses" refers to the expressions arising from the pride of Hevajra <note>the practitioner identifying as the deity</note>, which are the recitation of the essence and the mantra. This is the highly condensed meaning. The phrase "drawn with the feet" refers to the tracks made in dust, mud, water, and so forth; this represents the mandala in a very abbreviated way. "Trod upon" means being pressed by Hevajra or being the support of Hevajra. Regarding the verbal root for "Mother"...

<summary>This page provides a commentary on tantric terminology, explaining that the deity arises from within the body and defining the qualities of a Buddha. It interprets symbolic figures like the washerwoman as metaphors for internal wisdom and the process of purification.</summary>
<keywords>Hevajra, dehasambhava, six qualities of lordship, ultimate truth, relative truth, mandala, mantra recitation, wisdom</keywords>

The "Vajra-Maiden" <term>Vajra-kanyā</term> is the most excellent among those families, intended because others do not utilize her. "Deity of one's own desire" means the one to be accomplished. "Born from another family" means born from a family other than one's own chosen deity <term>Iṣṭadevatā</term>. "Purified" means properly empowered; taking that, one should perform the conduct; thus it should be applied. "With joy" refers to the joy arising from yoga. "Vajra-possessor" <term>Vajrin</term> means that the Vajra is the indivisibility of the two truths; it means the "Vajra-Song" which expresses that. "By the Vajra-feet" refers to the hands, feet, the gaze of the face, and other mudras that clarify reality. "With the form of a wheel" means with the form of a wheel. "On the hand" refers to the bracelet on the forearm. "Purity of hatred" means with the form of Hevajra. "Purity of mantra" refers to the song of devotion to the mantra, taken as a song. "Dance" refers to performing the dance. "By the nature of meditation" means devotion to meditation itself. "Always sing songs and also perform dances"; thus it should be applied. B.text:
The one who desires <term>siddhi</term> <gloss>spiritual accomplishment</gloss> is defined as one who, through unremitting yoga and conduct, attains <term>Hevajra</term> <gloss>The Joyful Vajra</gloss> in this very life. The meaning is that if such diligence exists—that is, if there is joy—one will attain buddhahood. This is how the text should be applied. The <term>vajra</term> girl is the most excellent among those of her family <note>lineage or class</note>, intended in the sense that she is not used by others. The phrase personal chosen deity means one should achieve the practice. The phrase born from another family refers to those arising from a lineage other than one's own <term>yidam</term> <gloss>meditational deity</gloss>. Purified means properly empowered. This should be applied to the act of taking hold of and engaging in the practice. Through joy refers to the joy arising from yoga. Possessing the <term>vajra</term> means that the <term>vajra</term> is the inseparability of the two truths; the meaning is the <term>vajra</term> song that expresses that inseparability. Through <term>vajra</term> steps refers to the hands, feet, facial expressions, and other <term>mudras</term> <gloss>symbolic hand gestures</gloss> that clarify reality. In the form of a wheel means exactly that: in the form of a wheel. On the hand refers to the bracelets on the forearms. Purified hatred refers to the form of <term>Hevajra</term>. The purity of mantra is the song regarded as mantra, which is performed as a song. Dance means the act of dancing. By the nature of meditation means regarding it as meditation itself. This should be connected to the instruction to always sing and always dance. Always means at all times. Even death refers to the experience of dying. Will be protected means obtaining protection. Arisen from <term>Hum</term> is <term>Akshobhya</term> <gloss>The Unshakeable Buddha</gloss>. The skull cup which has the nature of <term>Akshobhya</term> and the others is the <term>Buddhakapala</term> <gloss>Buddha-Skull</gloss>. The hair sash is a waistband made of hair. Ash refers to being smeared with ashes. The hair purifier is worn as an offering for the hair. Craving, delusion, and so forth are obstacles for the yogi and must be abandoned. Shame means the sense of embarrassment. Sleep is a great obstacle to yoga, and attachment to sustaining the body is also the root of a yogi's obstacles. Therefore, it is taught—

A.text: "Lord" means that even the Buddha is described as the master of the eleventh ground; thus it should be applied. If one wonders "how" with these grounds, "by these" means by the grounds of the sites and so forth. The mudras of the Ground of Practicing Devotion, the Joyous Ground, the Stainless Ground, and so forth, up to and including the Ground of Light, which are the grounds of primordial wisdom, are the sites and so forth as appropriate; such is the intention. "Others are inexpressible" means it is not because they are excluded from the sites and so forth; the intention is that the mudra and that which is sealed by the mudra are indivisible. "City" is Pāṭaliputra. The distinction of Harikela is the Salt Ocean and so forth. "Possessed of gold" is the Island of Gold <term>Suvarṇadvīpa</term>. "Proximity" means the vicinity of that. "Pond" refers to those staying in Narpa. "Hungry ghost" <term>Preta</term> "half-moon" means the end of the month. "Banner" is the graceful one. "Generating compassion" means thinking about the suffering of that very state. "By the wise" means by the learned. "Malicious" refers to those who hate the vehicle of mantra. "To make them enter" refers to the vehicle of mantra. "By that reason, all rituals" means all should be performed. "Principally" means by making them enter principally. Having spoken of compassion, wisdom <term>Prajñā</term> is also spoken: "In that..." and so forth. "Should be seen" means should be contemplated. Those two times are Hevajra and his Wisdom. Therefore, all actions gathered by that are virtuous. Other methods are spoken: "nothing not to be done..." and so forth. "In this" refers to the pride of Hevajra. Just as one is devoted to oneself, it is the same for sentient beings; therefore, for the sake of genuine gathering, "oneself also" is the meaning. "Supreme self" refers to this very Blessed One, Hevajra. "Abiding in the stage" is for the sake of firm pride. Because of being

B.text:
The term Lord means the Buddha as well. This refers to the fact that the Buddha is the sovereign of the eleventh stage <note>original: bhūmi</note>, and is thus described in this way. Regarding the thought, "How do these stages function?"—the phrase "by these" refers to the stages of the dwelling places and so forth. 

The <term>mudras</term> <gloss>ritual hand gestures or symbolic seals</gloss> of the stages of primordial wisdom—including the Stage of Practicing with Devotion <note>original: adhimukticaryā-bhūmi</note>, the Joyous Stage <note>original: pramuditā-bhūmi</note>, the Stainless Stage <note>original: vimalā-bhūmi</note>, and so forth up to the Radiance Stage <note>original: samantaprabhā-bhūmi</note>—are established in their respective dwelling places as appropriate. This is the intended meaning. 

The phrase "nothing else can be said" does not mean that the dwelling places and so forth are excluded; rather, it means that the <term>mudra</term> and that which is sealed by the <term>mudra</term> are inseparable. 

The city is Pataliputra. The distinction of Harikela refers to the Salt Ocean and so forth. The Land of Gold refers to <term>Suvarnadvipa</term> <gloss>the Golden Isle, likely Sumatra or the Malay Peninsula</gloss>. The "environs" are called such because they are near to that place. The "pond" is situated in a long, narrow shape. The phrase "the half-moon of the <term>pretas</term> <gloss>hungry ghosts</gloss>" refers to the latter half of the month. The "banner" refers to the graceful one. "Generating compassion" means contemplating the very suffering of those beings. "By the wise" refers to the learned ones. "The malicious" are those who feel hatred toward the <term>Mantrayana</term> <gloss>Vehicle of Secret Mantra</gloss>. "In order to lead them in" means to lead them into the Vehicle of Secret Mantra. "By that reason, all rituals" means all rituals are to be performed. "As the principal" means by making it the primary focus. 

After compassion was taught, wisdom <note>original: prajñā</note> was also taught with the phrase "in that" and so forth. "Should be viewed" means it should be contemplated. Those two times are <term>Hevajra</term> <gloss>the "Joyful Vajra" deity</gloss> and his wisdom consort. Therefore, all actions gathered by that are virtuous. Other methods were taught in the phrase "nothing that should not be done" and so forth. 

"In this" refers to the divine pride of Hevajra. Just as one has great devotion for oneself, so it is for all sentient beings; therefore, to correctly gather them together, it says "oneself as well." "The supreme self" refers to this very Blessed Lord, meaning Hevajra. "Abiding in the state" is for the sake of making the divine pride firm.

<summary>This page provides a technical commentary on the stages of Buddhist realization and the symbolism of the deity Hevajra. It explains geographical locations, ritual mudras, and the integration of compassion and wisdom within the Secret Mantra tradition.</summary>
<keywords>Hevajra, bhūmi, mudra, Pataliputra, Suvarnadvipa, Mantrayana, compassion, divine pride, prajna</keywords>

A.text: Thus, meditation is not pointless; for if the perfection of meditation is lacking, it is impossible to make it manifest. As it has been said: "The path that extracts the thorn of existence was shown to you by me. The Tathagata is the shower; you must strive for yourselves." If so, for the path that transcends the world, it would follow that co-emergent joy is directly perceived by those who engage in desire. If even the oral instructions are pointless for that, what need to mention meditation? If one asks what is the use of another's oral instructions for a matter of direct perception, it is said: "Merit," and so forth. This is the intent: here, the worldly co-emergent joy itself is not the thing to be accomplished, because it is already established, and because it is inferior to the bliss of the higher and higher god realms, etc. Because it is accompanied by taints <note>Sanskrit: āsrava</note>, it is impurity itself, and thus it is the very root of the faults of those in cyclic existence. Then what is it like? That which is the individual perfect awareness of the Tathagatas, the co-emergent Dharma Body <note>Sanskrit: dharmakāya</note> which is like space, and the co-emergent Enjoyment Body <note>Sanskrit: sambhogakāya</note> which arises in accordance with its cause—the most excellent, perfectly pure co-emergent characterized by certain bliss—that is what is to be accomplished here. Furthermore, since it is not realized by other means, the perfection of meditation through superior devotion to the oral instructions on the worldly co-emergent joy itself leads to manifestation, which is known by oneself. It is not so from the very beginning; therefore, hearing, contemplation, and meditation are not pointless here. "Method" is the path. "Relying on that" is authentic meditation. "Succession of many" means many types. "Obtained from the Guru" refers to the Guru's timing; the Guru should bestow it according to the ritual to a student who is a suitable vessel for the lineage; this is the meaning of "bestowing the pith instructions."

will occur. Thus, meditation is not without purpose, because without the total perfection of meditation, one is unable to manifest that <note>realization</note> directly. As it has been said:

The path that removes the thorns of existence
I have shown to you.
The <term>Tathagata</term> <gloss>One Gone Thus; the Buddha</gloss> is the teacher;
You must strive for it yourselves.

One might ask: "If the <term>Sahaja-ananda</term> <gloss>innate joy</gloss> of this world is already direct experience for those who engage in desire, then instruction is unnecessary, let alone meditation. What use is another's instruction for something that is already a direct object of experience?" To this, the text says: "Virtue," and so forth.

This is the intention: here, the innate joy of the world is not what is to be accomplished. It is already established, it is inferior to the bliss of higher realms such as the god realms, and because it possesses <term>asrava</term> <gloss>defilements or taints</gloss>, it is the very root of the faults of those in <term>samsara</term> <gloss>the cycle of suffering</gloss>. 

If one asks: "Then what is the nature of it?" Here, that which is to be accomplished is the <term>Dharmakaya</term> <gloss>Truth Body</gloss> which is the individual pristine awareness of the <term>Tathagatas</term>, innate like space, and the exceptionally sublime, utterly pure, and definitive characteristic of innate bliss that arises as the <term>Sambhogakaya</term> <gloss>Enjoyment Body</gloss>, which is its natural expression.

Furthermore, since this cannot be realized by other means, one understands it for oneself by manifesting the perfection of meditation. This is achieved through the power of devoted interest, following the instructions exactly as they pertain to the world's own innate joy. This does not happen from the very beginning. Therefore, in this context, listening <note>to the teachings</note>, contemplating, and meditating are not without purpose.

"Method" refers to the path. "Relying upon it" refers to authentic meditation. "The lineage of many of these" refers to many different types <note>of methods</note>. "Obtained from the Guru" refers to the Guru's timing; the Guru should bestow this in accordance with the ritual to a student who is a suitable vessel for the lineage. This is the meaning of "bestowing the instructions." Regarding that which is to be realized <unclear>...</unclear>

<summary>This page explains that while worldly pleasure is innate, it is a source of suffering and differs from the innate bliss of a Buddha. Realization of the Truth Body and Enjoyment Body requires systematic meditation, contemplation, and authentic instruction from a Guru.</summary>
<keywords>innate joy, Sahaja, Dharmakaya, Sambhogakaya, meditation, Guru, lineage, Tathagata, desire, purification</keywords>

A.text:
and so forth. Regarding the phrase "Even a man of little merit," it refers to someone who did not accumulate merit in previous lives. "There is no doubt he will succeed" means success comes because this yoga itself accumulates merit. The word "eating" refers to the time of consuming food. "Even while sleeping"
<margin>sleeping</margin>
means that through constant training, one will see the truth in a similar way even within dreams. "Entering the stream" refers to the spontaneous attainment of "Equal Taste" through this very yoga. If one asks what is achieved by this continual practice, it is said: "The Great Seal" <term>Mahamudra</term> and so forth, meaning it is intended for the sake of attaining the accomplishments <term>siddhi</term> of the Great Seal. It is explained that merit is created by the system of those who are exceptionally devoted to such yoga. To explain the mental offering of aspiration, it is said: "In this way," and so forth. "All beings" refers to both sentient beings and the physical environment <note>literally: the vessel world</note>.
All these should be meditated upon as one. If one wonders why they should be grasped with certainty, it is said: "by the mind," and so forth. The "mind" is the consciousness that conceptualizes; however, the truth is not to be analyzed by that conceptual mind, yet it is through the mind that it must be grasped with certainty.
If one wonders: "If it is not to be analyzed, should one then not meditate?" To this it is said: "All phenomena," and so forth. Meditation is the thorough knowledge of all phenomena itself; it is not the conceptualization of them. One should understand that conceptual thoughts are by nature delusional.
If one asks what that thorough knowledge is like, it is said: "Analysis and," and so forth. The word "and" includes trees, mountains, oceans, and living creatures. All these are to be meditated upon as the supreme ultimate reality. It is described as a variety of things within the ultimate reality of one's devotion, but it is not the conceptualization of various aspects. If one asks what that supreme ultimate reality is, it is said: "By myself," and so forth. "Myself" refers to one's own mind. Its essence is "thatness" <term>tattva</term>, and it is from that very nature that

B.text:
<meta>continues from previous page</meta>
and so forth. Regarding the phrase **even by a person of little merit**, this refers to those who did not accumulate merit in their previous lives. The statement **there is no doubt they will achieve success** refers to the fact that merit is accumulated through this very yoga. Regarding the term **eating**, it means while in the act of consuming food. The phrase **even while sleeping** refers to the fact that through constant training, one will likewise see <note>meaning the realization or deity</note> even in dreams. **Entering the stream** refers to the effortless arising of the <term>rasa</term> <gloss>essential taste or sapidity</gloss> through this yoga.

If one asks what should be done with this continuous practice, the text says **The Great Seal** <note>original: "Mahamudra"</note> and so forth, meaning it is intended for the sake of the <term>siddhi</term> <gloss>attainment</gloss> of the Great Seal. Through the treatise that expresses great devotion to such a yoga, the accumulation of merit is explained.

To explain the making of mental aspirations, the text says **In this way** and so forth. **All wandering beings** refers to both the sentient beings and the external vessel of the world. All of these are to be meditated upon as a single unity. Regarding the question of why one should hold this certain understanding, the text says **by the mind** and so forth. The **mind** is the consciousness that forms conceptual constructions; it is not through that conceptualizing mind that the truth is to be examined, yet it is with that mind that the certain understanding must be held. This is the meaning.

If one thinks, "If it is not to be examined conceptually, should it then not be meditated upon?" the text therefore says **all phenomena** and so forth. Meditation is the thorough knowledge of phenomena itself; it is not the conceptualization. This is the meaning. The intention is that conceptual thoughts are by their very nature delusive.

Regarding what that thorough knowledge is like at that time, the text says **examination and** and so forth. The word **and so forth** includes trees, mountains, oceans, and living beings. All of these are to be meditated upon as the supreme <term>tattva</term> <gloss>reality or suchness</gloss>. It is described as various within the reality of devoted interest, but it is not a variety of conceptual constructions. Furthermore, if one asks how that is the supreme reality, the text therefore says **by myself** and so forth. **Myself** refers to one's own mind. Its **entity** is that very thing, namely its own essential nature.

<summary>This page discusses the effectiveness of yoga for practitioners regardless of past merit and explains how to meditate on the unity of the world and mind as the Great Seal. It distinguishes between delusive conceptual thoughts and the non-conceptual thorough knowledge of reality.</summary>
<keywords>merit, Great Seal, Mahamudra, meditation, mind, reality, tattva, conceptualization</keywords>

A.text:
Through that, one will directly experience the innate. By abiding in that, the yogi will accomplish the attainment <term>siddhi</term> of the Great Seal <term>mahāmudrā</term>. What is it like? He is a yogi of the Seal. Because he has been made suitable, he accomplishes the attainment of the Great Seal endowed with knowledge <term>vidyā</term>. Accomplishing the characteristic is the primary cause, while the application of the Seal is the simultaneous condition <term>sahakāri-pratyaya</term>, because here it is the pledge <term>samaya</term>. The attainment of knowledge and the person, and the attainment of the Great Seal, are the attainment of the person of the family <note>spiritual lineage</note>; for here, without the knowledge of the family, realization is impossible. 

At the time of the first three meditative absorptions, this is not intended, for at those times, there is only distraction. "In this way" means: in this way the empowerment <term>abhiṣeka</term> is to be given, and in this way also the yogi is to be accomplished through the Seal. For this purpose, the mandala is spoken of for the sake of empowering the student and for the sake of accomplishing the attainment. This refers to the Mandala of the Pledge and the Mandala of Accomplishment; that is what is meant by "it was shown." 

The specific mandalas like the "four pairs" and so forth are all easy to understand. "To be placed in the east" means to arrange them. By the words "the Lord of the Mandala" and so forth, the preliminary ritual service <term>sevā</term> is explained. "Of the mandala [deities]" refers to each individual deity of the mandala. "The words spoken" refers to: <term>oṃ vajra rakṣa rakṣa hūṃ phaṭ svāhā</term>. "Previously" means prior to purifying the ground. "The mantra beginning with A" refers to the mantra: <term>oṃ akāro mukhaṃ sarva dharmāṇāṃ ādyānutpannatvāt oṃ āḥ hūṃ phaṭ svāhā</term> <gloss>Om, the letter A is the door to all phenomena, because they are unarisen from the beginning, Om Ah Hum Phat Svaha</gloss>. "Protection" refers to the fence, the lattice, and so forth. "By this" means that even while drawing, one should make offerings and prayers to the Guru. "In this" refers to the support mandala that has been drawn. "Vajrasattva" means a stable mind; one is proud with that. "Extending the right" means extending the right leg. "Leg" refers to the lower leg. "Mandala" means in the mandala. "Later, the reality" means
