<meta>continues from previous page</meta>
...who have attained the stage of Buddhahood and found detachment, to all those Protectors, I urge them to turn the unsurpassed wheel of the Dharma.

To those who intend to demonstrate the final passing into nirvana, I join my palms in prayer and beseech them to remain for as many eons as there are atoms in the world, for the sake of the benefit and happiness of all beings.

Whatever slight merit I have accumulated through prostrating, offering, confessing, rejoicing, urging, and beseeching, I dedicate it all toward the cause of Enlightenment.

May offerings be made to the Buddhas of the past and to those residing in the worlds of the ten directions. May those who have not yet come swiftly fulfill their intentions and progress through the stages of Buddhahood.

May as many world-realms as exist in the ten directions become vast and completely pure. May they be filled with Victorious Ones who have gone to the seat of the Great Bodhi Tree and with the Sons of the Buddha.

May as many sentient beings as exist in the ten directions be eternally free from sickness and be happy. May the Dharma-related goals of all beings be met, and may their hopes be fulfilled.

While I practice the conduct of Enlightenment, may I remember my successive lives in all states of being. In all my lifetimes, from death to rebirth, may I always embrace the renunciate life.

Following in the footsteps of all the Victorious Ones, may I perfect the practice of exceptionally good conduct. Practicing pure and stainless ethical discipline, may I always act without failing or committing a fault.

In the language of the gods, the <term>Nagas</term> <gloss>serpent spirits</gloss>, and the <term>Yakshas</term> <gloss>nature spirits</gloss>; in the language of the <term>Kumbhandas</term> <gloss>ghouls</gloss> and of human beings—in as many sounds as there are among all living beings, I shall teach the Dharma in every language.

Through that, may I be diligent in the Perfections <note>Paramitas</note> and never forget the Mind of Enlightenment <note>Bodhicitta</note>. May whatever sins act as obscurations be completely purified without exception.

May I be liberated from karma, mental afflictions, and the works of the <term>Mara</term> <gloss>the tempter or demonic forces</gloss>, and move through the worlds of beings...

B.text:
The lamps of the world <note>a poetic epithet for Buddhas</note>, through the stages of enlightenment, have attained non-attachment and Buddhahood. I urge all those protectors to turn the supreme wheel of Dharma. To those who intend to demonstrate the final passing into nirvana, I pray with palms pressed together: please remain for as many eons as there are atoms in the world, for the sake of the benefit and happiness of all wandering beings.

Whatever slight virtue I have accumulated through prostrating, offering, confessing, rejoicing, urging, and praying, I dedicate it all toward the attainment of enlightenment.

May offerings be made to the Buddhas of the past and to those residing in the worlds of the ten directions. May those who have not yet arrived quickly fulfill their intentions and come as Buddhas through the stages of enlightenment. May all the world realms in the ten directions become vast and completely pure. May they be filled with victors who have gone to the foot of the king of trees <note>the Bodhi tree where enlightenment is attained</note> and by the sons of the Buddhas <note>Bodhisattvas</note>.

May all the many sentient beings in the ten directions always be healthy and happy. May the meaningful Dharma goals of all beings be met, and may their hopes be fulfilled. As I practice the conduct of enlightenment, may I remember my births in all states of existence. In all successive lives, through death, transition, and birth, may I always renounce worldly life <note>take monastic vows</note>.

Following in the footsteps of all the victors, may I bring the <term>Samantabhadra-charya</term> <gloss>Conduct of Excellence</gloss> to perfection. May I always practice a flawless and stainless moral conduct, never declining and remaining free from faults.

In the languages of the gods, the <term>nagas</term> <gloss>serpent-beings</gloss>, and the <term>yakshas</term> <gloss>nature spirits</gloss>, in the languages of <term>kumbhandas</term> <gloss>ghoulish spirits</gloss> and of humans, in as many sounds as there are of all wandering beings, I shall teach the Dharma in all their tongues.

Through that, may I be diligent in the perfections and never forget the <term>bodhicitta</term> <gloss>the mind of enlightenment</gloss>. May whatever misdeeds act as obscurations be completely purified without exception. May I be liberated from karma, mental afflictions, and the works of demons <note>the four Maras</note>, and in all worldly wanderings...

...just as a lotus is not stained by water, or as the sun and moon travel through the sky without being hindered.

Throughout the extent of the realms and directions, may I pacify the suffering of the lower realms. May I establish all beings in happiness and act for the benefit of every living creature.

Perfecting the conduct of Enlightenment, I shall engage in a manner consistent with the behavior of sentient beings. Demonstrating exceptionally good conduct, I shall practice throughout all future eons.

May I always be accompanied by those whose conduct is similar to mine. Through body, speech, and also through mind, may we practice with the same conduct and aspirations.

May I always meet with those friends who wish to benefit me and who clearly demonstrate the path of exceptionally good conduct. May I never disappoint their hearts.

May I always personally behold the Victorious Protectors surrounded by the Sons of the Buddha. Throughout all future eons, without ever becoming weary, I shall make vast offerings to them.

Upholding the sacred Dharma of the Victorious Ones, I shall cause the conduct of Enlightenment to appear everywhere. Refining the practice of exceptionally good conduct, I shall practice throughout all future eons.

Even while wandering through all cycles of existence, may I find inexhaustible merit and wisdom. May I become an inexhaustible treasury of skillful means, wisdom, meditative absorption, liberation, and all excellent qualities.

On a single atom sit as many realms as there are atoms; in those realms sit inconceivable Buddhas. I shall behold them as they reside in the midst of the Sons of the Buddha, practicing the conduct of Enlightenment.

In this way, in all directions without exception, even within the space of a single hair, there are oceans of Buddhas of the three times, oceans of realms, and oceans of eons; I shall enter and practice within them.

Through the sounds of an ocean of melodic branches within a single word, which possesses the pure melodies of all the Victorious Ones, I shall always engage with the speech of the Buddha—a melody that accords with the inclinations of all beings.

All the Victorious Ones who have appeared in the three times...

I shall place all beings in happiness and act for the benefit of every living creature. I shall complete the conduct of enlightenment and engage in harmony with the activities of sentient beings. I shall demonstrate the conduct of excellence <note>original: "bhadracarya", referring to the practice of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra</note> and practice it throughout all future eons.

I shall always behold the Victorious Ones <gloss>Buddhas</gloss>, the Protectors surrounded by the Sons of the Buddha <gloss>Bodhisattvas</gloss>. Without ever growing weary throughout all future eons, I shall make vast offerings to them. I shall uphold the holy Dharma <gloss>teachings</gloss> of the Victorious Ones and cause the conduct of enlightenment to appear everywhere. I shall purify the conduct of excellence and practice it throughout all future eons.

With the sounds of the ocean of branches of a single speech, which possesses the pure melody of all the Victorious Ones, and with melodies that accord with the intentions of all beings, I shall always engage with the speech of the Buddha. ...continually turn the wheels of the Dharma; I too shall engage with their inexhaustible melodic speech through the power of my intelligence.

I shall enter into all future eons in a single instant. I shall practice by entering into whatever the measure of eons in the three times may be in just a fraction of a moment.

I shall behold in a single instant those who are the Lions among Men who appear in the three times. I shall always enter their sphere of activity through the power of miraculous liberation.

Whatever arrays of realms exist in the three times, I shall manifest them upon a single atom. Thus, I shall engage in the array of the realms of the Victorious Ones in every direction without exception.

I shall go before all the Protectors—those Lamps of the World who are yet to come, who will sequentially attain Buddhahood, turn the wheel, and demonstrate the final peace of nirvana.

Through the power of swift miracles, the power of the vehicle that is the door to all things, the power of conduct possessing every virtue, and the power of all-pervading loving-kindness;

Through the power of all-encompassing merit and virtue, the power of wisdom free from attachment, and the powers of wisdom, skillful means, and meditative absorption, I shall perfectly accomplish the powers of Enlightenment.

Completely purifying the power of karma, totally destroying the power of mental afflictions, rendering the power of the <term>Maras</term> <gloss>demonic forces</gloss> powerless, I shall perfect the power of exceptionally good conduct.

Purifying oceans of realms, liberating oceans of sentient beings, seeing clearly oceans of phenomena, and realizing oceans of wisdom;

Purifying oceans of conduct, fulfilling oceans of prayers, making offerings to oceans of Buddhas, I shall practice without weariness for oceans of eons.

A.text:

...of the Victorious Ones who have appeared in the three times, I shall fulfill them all without exception by becoming a Buddha through exceptionally good conduct.

The eldest son of all the Victorious Ones is called "Samantabhadra" <gloss>The Ever-Good One</gloss>. In order to practice as that wise one does, I dedicate all these virtues.

With pure body, speech, and mind, with pure conduct and completely pure realms, may I be just like that wise one in his excellent dedication.

In order to practice the good conduct that is entirely virtuous, I shall practice the prayer of Manjushri. Without becoming weary throughout all future eons, I shall fulfill his activities without exception.

May my conduct be without limit. May my excellent qualities also be beyond measure. By dwelling in immeasurable conduct, may I understand all their miraculous manifestations.

As far as the ends of space reach, so too do the ends of all sentient beings. As far as the ends of karma and mental afflictions reach, so too is the limit of my prayer.

Whoever hears this Sovereign of Dedications and, longing for supreme Enlightenment, develops faith for even a single moment, will gain the most excellent and supreme merit.

Whoever makes this prayer for exceptionally good conduct will abandon all lower realms. They will have abandoned evil companions and will soon behold the Buddha of Infinite Light <note>Amitabha</note>.

They will gain great boons and live in happiness. Even in this human life, things will go well for them. They will soon become just like Samantabhadra himself.

B.text:
As for the specific prayers for the conduct of the enlightened ones, those Victors who have gone before: through the conduct of the <term>Samantabhadra</term> <gloss>the Universal Goodness</gloss>, after I attain the awakening of a Buddha, I shall fulfill them all completely without exception.

The eldest son of all the Victors, whose name is called <term>Samantabhadra</term> <gloss>Ever-Excellent</gloss>; in order to practice in a way equal to that wise one, I dedicate all these virtues. 

May my body, speech, and mind also be completely pure; may my conduct be pure, and the realms be entirely pure. Just as the wise one is in his excellent dedication, may I also become equal to him.

In order to practice the excellent virtue in all ways, I shall practice the prayer of <term>Manjushri</term> <gloss>Gentle Glory, the Bodhisattva of Wisdom</gloss>. Without becoming weary throughout all future eons, I shall fulfill his activities completely without exception.

May my conduct be without any limit. May my qualities also be beyond measure. By remaining within this limitless conduct, I shall come to know all their miraculous transformations.

To whatever extent the limits of space reach, the limits of sentient beings are likewise without exception. To whatever extent <term>karma</term> <gloss>actions and their effects</gloss> and <term>kleshas</term> <gloss>mental afflictions</gloss> reach their limit, so shall be the limit of my prayers.

Whoever takes the infinite realms of the ten directions, adorns them with jewels, and offers them to the Victors—and even offers the supreme joys of gods and humans for eons as numerous as the atoms of those realms—if they should hear this King of Dedications and, being greatly inspired toward supreme awakening, feel faith for even a single moment, they will gain a merit far more supreme and holy than that.

Whoever makes this Prayer of Excellent Conduct will abandon all lower realms of existence. Such a person has abandoned negative friends and will quickly see <term>Amitabha</term> <gloss>the Buddha of Boundless Light</gloss>. 

They will gain great findings and live in happiness. Even in this human life, things will go well for them. In a short time, they will become just like <term>Samantabhadra</term> himself.

Whatever sins of the five inexpiable crimes <note>The five most serious sins in Buddhism: killing one's father, killing one's mother, killing an Arhat, drawing the blood of a Buddha, and causing a schism in the Sangha.</note> were committed under the power of ignorance, by reciting this Excellent Conduct <unclear>it is purified.</unclear>

<summary>This passage continues the Prayer of Samantabhadra, emphasizing the dedication of merit and the immense spiritual benefits of reciting the prayer. It promises the purification of even the heaviest sins and the eventual attainment of Buddhahood through the imitation of Samantabhadra and Manjushri.</summary>
<keywords>Samantabhadra, Manjushri, Bodhisattva Path, Dedication of Merit, Amitabha, Five Inexpiable Crimes, Universal Goodness, Enlightenment</keywords>

A.text:
<meta>continues from previous page</meta>
they will be swiftly and completely purified without exception.

They will be endowed with wisdom, a beautiful form, the marks of excellence, a good family, and a radiant complexion. Many demons and heretics will not be able to overcome them. They will be honored in all three worlds.

They will swiftly go to the seat of the Great Bodhi Tree. Having gone there, they will stay for the benefit of sentient beings, attain Enlightenment, turn the wheel of Dharma, and subdue all the <term>Maras</term> <gloss>demons</gloss> together with their hosts.

The full maturation <note>the karmic result</note> for whoever upholds, teaches, or reads this prayer of exceptionally good conduct is known only by the Buddha. Do not have any doubt regarding supreme Enlightenment.

Just as Manjushri is brave in his knowledge, and Samantabhadra is the same, I shall train following in the footsteps of them all and dedicate all these virtues.

With that dedication which is praised as supreme by all the Victorious Ones who appear in the three times, I dedicate all these roots of my virtue toward exceptionally good conduct.

When the time of my death comes, may all my obscurations be cleared away. Having directly beheld the Buddha of Infinite Light <note>Amitabha</note>, may I go to that realm of Sukhavati <gloss>The Blissful Land</gloss>.

Having gone there, may all these very prayers be manifested without exception. I shall fulfill them all without remainder and act for the benefit of sentient beings as long as the world exists.

In that excellent and joyful mandala of the Victorious One, may I be born from a very beautiful and supreme lotus. May I personally receive a prophecy <note>of future Buddhahood</note> from the Victorious One of Infinite Light.

Having received that prophecy there, may I benefit sentient beings in many ways through the power of my intelligence, using hundreds of millions of emanations in all the ten directions.

Whatever slight merit I have accumulated by reciting the prayer of exceptionally good conduct, may the virtuous prayers of all beings be fulfilled by it in a single instant.

B.text:
<meta>continues from previous page</meta>
If spoken, one will quickly and completely become purified without exception. One will possess primordial wisdom, a physical form, and the marks of excellence, along with the proper family and complexion. Many demons and <term>tirthikas</term> <gloss>non-Buddhist extremists</gloss> will be unable to overcome such a person. They will be honored throughout all the three worlds.

They will quickly go to the foot of the king of Bodhi trees. Having gone there, they will sit for the benefit of sentient beings, attain enlightenment as a Buddha, and turn the wheel of Dharma. They will subdue all the demons together with their hosts.

The ripening result for anyone who holds, teaches, or reads this Prayer of Excellent Conduct is known only by the Buddha. Do not have any doubt regarding supreme enlightenment.

Just as the heroic Manjushri knows, and Samantabhadra does as well, I will train myself following after them and dedicate all these virtues completely. With that dedication which is praised as supreme by all the Victors who have departed in the three times, I also dedicate all these roots of my virtue for the sake of excellent conduct.

When the time comes for me to die, by clearing away all obscurations and perceiving Amitabha <note>original: "Snang ba mtha' yas", the Buddha of Infinite Light</note> directly, may I go to that realm of Sukhavati <note>original: "Bde ba can", the Land of Bliss</note>.

Having gone there, may all these prayers be manifest without exception. I will fulfill them all entirely and act for the benefit of sentient beings as long as the world remains.

In that excellent and joyful mandala of the Victor, born from a most beautiful and holy lotus, may I receive a prophecy directly from the Victor Amitabha. Having received that prophecy there, may I bring much benefit to sentient beings in the ten directions through the power of the mind, using hundreds of millions of numerous emanations.

Through whatever slight virtue I have accumulated by reciting the Prayer of Excellent Conduct, may all the virtuous prayers of beings be accomplished in a single instant.

"What should one say to bring about well-being?" 
When he heard these words, the Kinsman of the World <note>an epithet for the Buddha</note> spoke:

In this world, in others, and in the heavens, 
Whatever wonderful, vast, and supreme jewels exist,
They cannot match, count, or even equal 
The jewel of the Perfect Buddha.
This is an exceedingly wonderful and immeasurable marvel:
The jewel of the Perfect Buddha is the supreme of the world.
Just as this of mine is the supreme truth,
By this truth, may there be great well-being!
The cessation of peace, the nectar that is truly excellent,
Which the Sage of the Shakyas <note>Shakyamuni Buddha</note> realized in meditative absorption;
There is nothing equal to that Dharma.
Having realized it, one is henceforth without sorrow.
This is an exceedingly wonderful and immeasurable marvel:
The Sublime Dharma is the supreme jewel of the world.
Just as this of mine is the supreme truth,
By this truth, may there be great well-being!
The Victors have spoken of the eight types of individuals,
Who comprise the four pairs of persons <note>the four pairs of Noble Beings: those entering and abiding in the fruits of Stream-enterer, Once-returner, Non-returner, and Arhat</note>.
These worthy objects of offerings are very rare on this earth.
Giving to them results in immeasurable merit.
This is an exceedingly wonderful and immeasurable marvel:
The jewel of the Sangha is the supreme of the world.
Just as this of mine is the supreme truth,

The Sublime One, the Great One, the giver of supreme excellence,

The supreme of the supreme of holy wisdom,

The jewel of the Perfect Buddha is the supreme of the world.

This is an exceedingly wonderful and immeasurable marvel:

Just as this of mine is the supreme truth,
By this truth, may there be great well-being!

A.text:
firm and very secure,
Unmoved by the four great powerful winds,
Likewise, the wise person who remains seeing the Four Truths
Cannot be shaken by the speakers of the world.
This is an exceedingly wonderful and immeasurable marvel:
The jewel of the Sangha is the supreme of the world.
Just as this of mine is the supreme truth,
By this truth, may there be great well-being!
The Subduer of all, the All-Knowing, the All-Seeing,
Possessing all the powers of omniscience,
The supreme of all, free from all grasping,
The Knower of all intentions, this is the unique Blessed One.
This is an exceedingly wonderful and immeasurable marvel:
The jewel of the Perfect Buddha is the supreme of the world.
Just as this of mine is the supreme truth,
By this truth, may there be great well-being!
It stops cyclic existence, is immovable and unchanging,
Faultless, and completely liberated from all fears.
Perfectly ceased and excellent, it is the certain emergence.
Utterly stainless and peaceful, it cannot be stolen by the intellect.
This is an exceedingly wonderful and immeasurable marvel:
The jewel of the Sublime Dharma is the supreme of the world.
Just as this of mine is the supreme truth,
By this truth, may there be great well-being!
Those who point out great suffering and bestow happiness,
Who see the Truths and are conscientious,
Who are without doubt regarding the Jewel Truths—
They will not take an eighth birth <note>referring to a Stream-enterer who is guaranteed enlightenment within seven lifetimes</note>.
This is an exceedingly wonderful and immeasurable marvel:
The jewel of the Sangha is the supreme of the world.
Just as this of mine is the supreme truth,
By this truth, may there be great well-being!
The supreme of the sublime ones, who knows the ultimate truth,
Knowing the supreme and the non-supreme, striving for the ultimate,
Not to be stolen by others, realizing the sublime mind,
The supreme protector of those in great suffering.
This is an exceedingly wonderful and immeasurable marvel:
The jewel of the Perfect Buddha is the supreme of the world.
Just as this of mine is the supreme truth,
By this truth, may there be great well-being!
Having generated aspiration and becoming endowed with yoga,
Always striving in the teaching of Gautama and being fully liberated,
They touch that pure land which is not led by others.

<summary>This page contains verses of praise and aspiration centered on the Three Jewels and the Four Noble Truths. It emphasizes the stability of the wise and the power of truth to bring well-being and liberation from rebirth.</summary>
<keywords>Three Jewels, Buddha, Dharma, Sangha, Four Noble Truths, liberation, well-being, Gautama, yoga</keywords>

A.text:
That which touches this cannot be reached by counting.
This is an exceedingly wonderful and immeasurable marvel:
The jewel of the Sangha is the supreme of the world.
Just as this of mine is the supreme truth,
By this truth, may there be great well-being!
By seeing the Truth and speaking of it, if by any chance
Some sin should be committed,
It is not right for that person to conceal it;
Because this nature of reality remains immovable.
This is an exceedingly wonderful and immeasurable marvel:
The jewel of the Sangha is the supreme of the world.
Just as this of mine is the supreme truth,
By this truth, may there be great well-being!
In all the worlds including the gods,
There is no one superior or equal to the Buddha.
The unsurpassed Teacher of gods and humans,
The Teacher, the Guide, the supreme among physicians.
This is an exceedingly wonderful and immeasurable marvel:
The jewel of the Perfect Buddha is the supreme of the world.
Just as this of mine is the supreme truth,
By this truth, may there be great well-being!
In the first month of summer, when the Sage
Attained the supreme Dharma in the forest,
There was nothing superior or equal to that Dharma.
That which touches this cannot be reached by counting.
This is an exceedingly wonderful and immeasurable marvel:
The jewel of the Sublime Dharma is the supreme of the world.
Just as this of mine is the supreme truth,
By this truth, may there be great well-being!
The old sins are withered and no new ones are made;
Free from the fear of chronic disease and beyond sorrow.
With the root ceased, they do not produce existence,
And the teaching will blaze like a lamp.
This is an exceedingly wonderful and immeasurable marvel:
The jewel of the Sangha is the supreme of the world.
Just as this of mine is the supreme truth,
By this truth, may there be great well-being!
The Verses of Well-being Requested by a Deity are complete.

In the language of India: <term>Svastyayana Gatha</term>
In the language of Tibet: <term>Bde legs su gyur pa'i tshigs su bcad pa</term> <gloss>Verses for Becoming Well-off</gloss>
Homage to the All-Knowing One.
A certain deity went near
To the presence of the Guide of the World,
And my request is:
"What is always well-being?"

B.text:
This will not be counted among those things touched.
It is an immeasurable and most marvelous wonder:
The Precious Community <note>original: "dge 'dun rin chen", referring to the Sangha</note> is the supreme in the world.
By the supreme truth of these words of mine,
May there be great well-being through this truth!
If one has seen the truth and spoken it, even if some sin
Has been committed on the path,
It is not appropriate to conceal it;
Because this nature of things <term>dharmata</term> <gloss>the intrinsic nature of reality</gloss> remains unmoving.
It is an immeasurable and most marvelous wonder:
The Precious Community is the supreme in the world.
By the supreme truth of these words of mine,
May there be great well-being through this truth!
In all the worlds including the realms of the gods,
There is none superior or equal to the Buddha.
He is the unsurpassed teacher of gods and men,
The supreme teacher, the caravan leader, and the physician.
It is an immeasurable and most marvelous wonder:
The Precious Perfect Buddha is the supreme in the world.
By the supreme truth of these words of mine,
May there be great well-being through this truth!
In the first month of summer, the Sage <note>referring to the Buddha, Shakyamuni</note>
Found the supreme Dharma in the forest groves.
There is none superior or equal to that Dharma.
This will not be counted among those things touched.
It is an immeasurable and most marvelous wonder:
The Precious Sublime Dharma is the supreme in the world.
By the supreme truth of these words of mine,
May there be great well-being through this truth!
Sins are withered and exhausted, and no new ones are made.
Without the disease of infectious fever, one is fearless and free from sorrow.
With the root ceased, existence is no longer produced;
The teaching will burn bright like a lamp.
It is an immeasurable and most marvelous wonder:
The Precious Community is the supreme in the world.
By the supreme truth of these words of mine,
May there be great well-being through this truth!

The Verses of Well-being Requested by a Deity are complete.

{D4401} In the language of India: <term>Svastayana-gatha</term> <gloss>Verses of Well-being</gloss>.
In the language of Tibet: <term>Bde legs su gyur pa'i tshigs su bcad pa</term>.
Homage to the All-Knowing One!
A certain deity approached
The Presence of the Leader of the World,
And asked: "What is that
Which is always well-being?"
